title: حِكَايَةُ وَزِيرِ الْمَلِكِ يُونَانَ
titleEn: The Story of King Yunan's Vizier, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 30–38 (continuing directly from nights-04, whose text ends with King Yunan hotly defending Duban against his vizier's insinuations), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the project’s own two-pass-plus-adjudication pipeline; the edition’s own OCR is unusable. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition’s — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, its several inconsistent spellings of the same word within this very night, and its occasional compositor’s slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized automatically once this file is published, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 5 completes the tale King Yunan tells the efrit. Defending his physician Duban against his vizier’s jealous insinuations, King Yunan tells his own cautionary tale, “The Story of King al-Sindibad”: a king who kills his loyal falcon in a fit of anger, only to discover a moment later that the bird had been trying to save him from a venomous snake dripping poison into his drinking water — and is overcome with too-late regret. The vizier answers with a cautionary tale of his own, of a treacherous vizier who strands a prince in the wilderness to be devoured by a ghouleh; the prince’s prayer saves him, and the treacherous vizier is executed once exposed. Persuaded by the parallel, King Yunan turns on Duban after all, over the sage’s repeated pleas and several gnomic verses — some the narrator’s own aside on submitting to fate, one Duban’s bitter lament at being repaid loyalty with betrayal. Duban is beheaded, but not before arranging one final trick: an ancient book that will make his severed head speak once the king opens it. The book’s pages are poisoned; King Yunan, wetting his finger to turn them, is fatally poisoned in turn, and Duban’s head recites a closing verse on tyrants overtaken by their own tyranny before the king falls dead. The fisherman — narrating all of this to the efrit he has trapped, one frame level further out — draws the moral explicitly: had King Yunan spared Duban, God would have spared him, and had you, O efrit, spared me, God would have spared you. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language toward Classical Arabic here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit. The night is frank about violent death and is translated that way.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ قَالَتْ لَهَا أُخْتُهَا أَتِمِّي لَنَا حَدِيثَكِ إِنْ كُنْتِ غَيْرَ نَايِمَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisatu qālat lahā ukhtuhā atimmī lanā ḥadīthaki in kunti ghayra nāyimatin
sentences.l: Then, when it was the fifth night, her sister said to her, 'Complete for us your story, if you are not asleep.'
sentences.i: When the fifth night came, her sister said to her, 'Finish the tale for us, if you are not yet asleep.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ يُونَانَ قَالَ لِوَزِيرِهِ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ أَنْتَ دَاخَلَكَ الْحَسَدُ مِنْ أَجْلِ هَذَا الْحَكِيمِ وَتُرِيدُ قَتْلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-malika Yūnāna qāla li-wazīrihi ayyuhā al-wazīru anta dākhalaka al-ḥasadu min ajli hādhā al-ḥakīmi wa-turīdu qatlahu
sentences.l: So she said: 'It has reached me, O fortunate king, that King Yunan said to his vizier: "O vizier, envy has entered into you on account of this sage, and you want his killing [i.e. to kill him]."'
sentences.i: So she said, 'It has reached me, O happy King, that King Yunan said to his vizier, "O vizier, envy has come over you on account of this sage, and you wish to kill him —"'
sentences.n: دَاخَلَكَ الْحَسَدُ (lit. 'envy has entered into you') uses the Form III verb دَاخَلَ idiomatically for a feeling taking possession of someone, as in دَاخَلَهُ الشَّكُّ, 'doubt came over him.'

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَنْدَمُ كَمَا نَدِمَ الْمَلِكُ السِّنْدِبَادُ عَلَى قَتْلِ الْبَازِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika andamu kamā nadima al-maliku al-Sindibādu ʿalā qatli al-bāzi
sentences.l: 'and after that I will regret [it], just as King al-Sindibad regretted the killing of the falcon.'
sentences.i: '— and afterward I shall regret it, just as King al-Sindibad regretted killing the falcon.'
sentences.n: أَنْدَمُ continues King Yunan's own speech to the vizier (begun in the previous sentence): it is a first-person imperfect ('I will regret'), the king predicting his own future remorse if he heeds the vizier's envy and has Duban killed — which is exactly what later comes to pass in the frame story. The bare rasm اندم gives no hint of person; the hamza of the 1st-person prefix (hamzat al-muḍāriʿ) is supplied here as elsewhere. This sentence is also the hinge that launches the embedded tale: the vizier's puzzled question in the next line lets King Yunan tell 'The Story of King al-Sindibad' as a cautionary parallel to his own situation.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ الْعَفْوَ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ وَكَيْفَ كَانَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru al-ʿafwa yā malika al-zamāni wa-kayfa kāna dhālika
sentences.l: The vizier said: 'Pardon, O king of the age! And how was that?'
sentences.i: The vizier said, 'Your pardon, O king of the age — and how was that?'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku
sentences.l: The king said:

sentences.t: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ السِّنْدِبَانِ
sentences.tr: ḥikāyatu al-maliki al-Sindibāni
sentences.l: The Story of King al-Sindibān
sentences.i: The Story of King al-Sindibān
sentences.n: This is the edition's own section heading, marking the start of the tale-within-the-tale that King Yunan tells his vizier. Note the spelling: here the name ends in ن (al-Sindibān), whereas every other occurrence in this same tale (and in nights-04) ends in د (al-Sindibād). Both spellings are printed in the source; each is vocalized and transliterated as its own occurrence gives it, rather than harmonized to one form.

sentences.t: حُكِيَ وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ مَلِكٌ مِنْ مُلُوكِ الْفُرْسِ وَكَانَ يُحِبُّ الْفَرَحَ وَالتَّنَزُّهَ وَالصَّيْدَ وَالْقَنَصَ
sentences.tr: ḥukiya wa-Allāhu aʿlamu annahu kāna malikun min mulūki al-Fursi wa-kāna yuḥibbu al-faraḥa wa-al-tanazzuha wa-al-ṣayda wa-al-qanaṣa
sentences.l: It is related — and God is most knowing — that there was a king among the kings of Persia, and he loved joy, and recreation, and hunting, and the chase.
sentences.i: It is told — and God knows best — that there was once a king among the kings of Persia who loved pleasure, going out for recreation, hunting, and the chase.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ مُرَبِّيَ بَازٍ لَا يُفَارِقُهُ لَيْلًا وَلَا نَهَارًا وَكَانَ طُولَ اللَّيْلِ شَائِلَهُ عَلَى يَدِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna murabbiya bāzin lā yufāriquhu laylan wa-lā nahāran wa-kāna ṭūla al-layli shāʾilahu ʿalā yadihi
sentences.l: And he was a raiser of a falcon that did not part from him by night nor by day, and he would be, the whole length of the night, keeping it perched upon his hand.
sentences.i: He kept a falcon he had raised, which never left him by night or by day, and all night long he would keep it perched upon his hand.
sentences.n: شَائِلَهُ ('keeping it raised/perched') is read as the active participle of شَالَ, 'to lift, hold aloft' — the falconer's fist held up with the bird on it — a plausible but somewhat technical sense for this root; the edition already prints the hamza on ي shown here (شائله), so it is kept exactly as given.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا طَلَعَ إِلَى الصَّيْدِ يَأْخُذُهُ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā ṭalaʿa ilā al-ṣaydi yaʾkhudhuhu maʿahu
sentences.l: and whenever he went out to the hunt, he would take it with him,
sentences.i: and whenever he rode out to hunt, he took it with him;

sentences.t: وَعَامَلَ لَهُ طَاسَةً مِنَ الذَّهَبِ مُعَلَّقَةً فِي رَقَبَتِهِ يَسْقِيهِ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ʿāmala lahu ṭāsatan mina al-dhahabi muʿallaqatan fī raqabatihi yasqīhi minhā
sentences.l: and he had made for it a cup of gold, hung about its neck, [from which] he would water it.
sentences.i: and he had a golden cup made for it, which hung about its neck, and from which he would give it to drink.
sentences.n: وَعَامَلَ is the Form III verb ʿāmala, Classically 'to deal with, treat'; here it is used in the looser colloquial sense still current in spoken Arabic, ʿāmal-lu ..., 'he had ... made/fixed up for him' — not the Classical meaning of the verb.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا الْمَلِكُ جَالِسٌ وَإِذَا بِأَمِيرِ الرَّخَةِ يَقُولُ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ هَذَا أَوَانُ الْخُرُوجِ لِلصَّيْدِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā al-maliku jālisun wa-idhā bi-amīri al-rakhati yaqūlu yā malika al-zamāni hādhā awānu al-khurūji lil-ṣaydi
sentences.l: So while the king was sitting, behold, the amīr of the rakha said: 'O king of the age, this is the time of going out to the hunt.'
sentences.i: Now while the king sat, an officer — the amīr of the rakha — suddenly announced, 'O king of the age, it is now time to ride out to the hunt.'
sentences.n: أَمِيرُ الرَّخَةِ ('the amīr/officer of the rakha') is obscure: no confirmed sense for الرخة in this title has been found in Lane or Hava, and it is vocalized here by best guess (as a plain triptote noun, without inventing an unattested doubled consonant) rather than corrected. It plausibly names a court or hunting official — perhaps the officer who announces the hour of departure — but the reading is offered with real uncertainty, not as a settled identification.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ بِالْخُرُوجِ وَأَخَذَ الْبَازَ عَلَى يَدِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-amara al-maliku bi-al-khurūji wa-akhadha al-bāza ʿalā yadihi
sentences.l: So the king commanded the going-out, and took the falcon upon his hand,
sentences.i: So the king gave the order to ride out, and took the falcon upon his hand,

sentences.t: وَسَارُوا إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى وَادٍ وَضَرَبُوا حَلْقَةَ الصَّيْدِ
sentences.tr: wa-sārū ilā an waṣalū ilā wādin wa-ḍarabū ḥalqata al-ṣaydi
sentences.l: and they journeyed until they arrived at a valley, and they pitched the ring of the hunt.
sentences.i: and they rode on until they reached a valley, where they formed the hunting-ring.
sentences.n: ضَرَبُوا حَلْقَةَ الصَّيْدِ ('they struck/pitched the hunting-ring') is the technical idiom for beaters and huntsmen forming a circle to drive game inward.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِغَزَالَةٍ وَقَعَتْ فِي حَلْقَةِ الصَّيْدِ فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ كُلُّ مَنْ نَطَّتِ الْغَزَالَةُ فَوْقَ دِمَاغِهِ قَتَلْتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-ghazālatin waqaʿat fī ḥalqati al-ṣaydi fa-qāla al-maliku kullu man naṭṭati al-ghazālatu fawqa dimāghihi qataltuhu
sentences.l: And behold, a gazelle fell [i.e. was caught] within the hunting-ring; so the king said: 'Whoever [it happens that] the gazelle jumps over his head, I kill him.'
sentences.i: And a gazelle was caught within the ring; so the king proclaimed, 'Whoever lets the gazelle leap over his head — I will kill him on the spot!'
sentences.n: قَتَلْتُهُ is a perfect verb used for immediate, certain future action in the response of a conditional — 'I kill him' standing for 'I shall surely kill him' — a common Classical idiom, distinct from the ordinary past-tense use of the perfect.

sentences.t: فَضَيَّقُوا عَلَيْهَا حَلْقَةَ الصَّيْدِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍayyaqū ʿalayhā ḥalqata al-ṣaydi
sentences.l: So they narrowed the hunting-ring upon her.
sentences.i: So they closed the ring in tighter around her.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِغَيْرِهَا دَخَلَتْ لِبَيْتِ الْمَلِكِ وَثَبَتَتْ عَلَى رِجْلَيْهَا وَحَطَّتْ يَدَيْهَا عَلَى صَدْرِهَا كَأَنَّهَا تَبُوسُ الْأَرْضَ لِلْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-ghayrihā dakhalat li-bayti al-maliki wa-thabatat ʿalā rijlayhā wa-ḥaṭṭat yadayhā ʿalā ṣadrihā ka-annahā tabūsu al-arḍa lil-maliki
sentences.l: And behold, another one of them entered into the king's tent, and stood firm upon her two legs, and set her two forelegs upon her chest, as if she were kissing the ground for the king.
sentences.i: And then another gazelle came right into the king's own pavilion, planted herself firmly on her legs, and set her forelegs upon her breast, as though she were kissing the ground before the king.

sentences.t: فَطَاطَاءَ الْمَلِكُ لِلْغَزَالَةِ فَفَرَّتْ مِنْ فَوْقِ دِمَاغِهِ رَاحَتْ لِلْبَرِّ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭāṭāʾa al-maliku lil-ghazālati fa-farrat min fawqi dimāghihi rāḥat lil-barri
sentences.l: So the king bowed [his head] to the gazelle; then she fled from over his head, [and] went off to the open country.
sentences.i: So the king bowed his head to her — and at that she darted away over his head and made off into the open wild.
sentences.n: طَاطَاءَ is a vernacular-shifted spelling of Classical طَأْطَأَ, 'to bow, lower the head': the medial hamza-with-sukūn has weakened to a long vowel (compare Classical رَأْس becoming dialectal رَاس), a common Middle Arabic/colloquial phonological shift. The edition's own final ء (rather than a seated hamza) is kept exactly as printed, following the ordinary orthographic rule that a hamza after a long alif is written bare on the line.

sentences.t: فَظَلَّ الْمَلِكُ رَأَى الْعَسْكَرَ يَتَغَامَزُونَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ يَا وَزِيرُ مَاذَا ذَا يَقُولُ الْعَسْكَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-ẓalla al-maliku raʾā al-ʿaskara yataghāmazūna ʿalayhi fa-qāla yā wazīru mādhā dhā yaqūlu al-ʿaskaru
sentences.l: So the king kept on: he saw the troops winking at one another over him; so he said: 'O vizier, what is this the troops are saying?'
sentences.i: The king then noticed the troops exchanging knowing glances about him, and said, 'Vizier, what is it the troops are saying?'
sentences.n: ظَلَّ is here followed directly by a perfect verb (رأى) rather than the Classical imperfect that ظَلَّ normally governs — a paratactic Middle Arabic construction, translated as a continuous 'kept on, went on [seeing]'. مَاذَا ذَا doubles the interrogative ('what... this') where Classical usage would need only مَاذَا; the second ذَا looks like a dittography, but is vocalized and rendered as printed rather than deleted.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّكَ قُلْتَ كُلُّ مَنْ نَطَّتِ الْغَزَالَةُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ يُقْتَلُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yaqūlūna innaka qulta kullu man naṭṭati al-ghazālatu fawqa raʾsihi yuqtalu
sentences.l: He said: 'They are saying: You said, whoever the gazelle jumps over his head is killed.'
sentences.i: He replied, 'They are saying that you declared, "Whoever lets the gazelle leap over his head shall be killed."'
sentences.n: يُقْتَلُ (passive, 'he is killed/shall be killed') recasts the king's own earlier first-person threat (قَتَلْتُهُ, 'I kill him', two sentences above) as an impersonal rule in the troops' report of it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ وَحَيَاةِ رَأْسِي لَأَتْبَعُهَا حَتَّى أَجِي بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku wa-ḥayāti raʾsī la-atbaʿuhā ḥattā ajī bihā
sentences.l: The king said: 'By the life of my head, I will surely follow her until I come with her [i.e. bring her back].'
sentences.i: The king said, 'By the life of my own head, I will follow her until I bring her back!'
sentences.n: أَجِي ('I come') is a colloquial/Middle Arabic form of Classical أَجِيءُ, the final root-hamza having weakened away entirely, as commonly happens in spoken Arabic (compare نَايِمَة for نَائِمَة, noted in nights-04); جَاءَ بِـ, 'to come with', is the ordinary idiom for 'to bring'.

sentences.t: فَظَلَّ الْمَلِكُ تَابِعَ الْغَزَالَةِ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ وَرَاءَهَا إِلَى جَبَلٍ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-ẓalla al-maliku tābiʿa al-ghazālati wa-lam yazal warāʾahā ilā jabalin mina al-jibāli
sentences.l: So the king kept following the gazelle, and did not cease [being] behind her, until [he came] to a mountain among the mountains.
sentences.i: So the king kept after the gazelle, never letting her out of his sight, until he came to one of the mountains,

sentences.t: فَأَرَادَتْ أَنْ تَعْبُرَ الْغَارَ
sentences.tr: fa-arādat an taʿbura al-ghāra
sentences.l: and she wanted to cross through the cave.
sentences.i: where she tried to slip through a cave.

sentences.t: فَسَيَّبَ الْبَازَ وَرَاءَهَا فَصَارَ يَلْطُشُهَا فِي عَيْنَيْهَا إِلَى أَنْ أَعْمَاهَا وَدَوَّخَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-sayyaba al-bāza warāʾahā fa-ṣāra yalṭushuhā fī ʿaynayhā ilā an aʿmāhā wa-dawwakhahā
sentences.l: So he released the falcon after her, and it began to strike at her in her two eyes, until it had blinded her and made her dizzy.
sentences.i: So the king let the falcon fly at her, and it fell to striking at her eyes, until it had blinded her and left her reeling.

sentences.t: فَسَحَبَ الْمَلِكُ دَبُّوسًا وَضَرَبَهَا قَلْبَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-saḥaba al-maliku dabbūsan wa-ḍarabahā qalbahā
sentences.l: So the king drew out a mace, and struck her — her heart —
sentences.i: So the king drew out his mace and struck her through the heart,

sentences.t: وَنَزَلَ ذَبَحَهَا وَسَلَخَهَا وَعَلَّقَهَا فِي قَرَبُوسِ السَّرْجِ
sentences.tr: wa-nazala dhabaḥahā wa-salakhahā wa-ʿallaqahā fī qarabūsi al-sarji
sentences.l: and he got down, slaughtered her, and skinned her, and hung her on the pommel of the saddle.
sentences.i: then dismounted, slaughtered her, skinned her, and hung her from the pommel of his saddle.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ سَاعَةَ قَيَالَةٍ وَكَانَتِ الْغَابَةُ مُقْفِرَةً لَمْ يُوجَدْ فِيهَا مَاءٌ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat sāʿata qayālatin wa-kānati al-ghābatu muqfiratan lam yūjad fīhā māʾun
sentences.l: And it was the hour of the midday rest, and the forest was desolate: no water was to be found in it.
sentences.i: It was now the hour of the midday rest, and the wilderness lay desolate around them, with no water anywhere to be found,
sentences.n: قَيَالَة is uncertain: the letters most plausibly represent a Middle Arabic/dialectal form of Classical قَيْلُولَة, 'midday rest, siesta' (compare the idiom سَاعَةَ الْقَائِلَة, 'the hour of noonday rest'), but the exact vocalization of this particular spelling is offered with genuine uncertainty rather than as a settled reading.

sentences.t: فَعَطِشَ الْمَلِكُ وَعَطِشَ الْحِصَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿaṭisha al-maliku wa-ʿaṭisha al-ḥiṣānu
sentences.l: so the king grew thirsty, and the horse grew thirsty.
sentences.i: so that both the king and his horse grew thirsty.

sentences.t: فَدَوَّرَ الْمَلِكُ فَرَأَى شَجَرَةً نَازِلًا مِنْهَا مَاءٌ مِثْلَ السَّمْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-dawwara al-maliku fa-raʾā shajaratan nāzilan minhā māʾun mithla al-samni
sentences.l: So the king searched about, and saw a tree, [with] water like clarified butter dripping down from it.
sentences.i: So the king cast about, and caught sight of a tree with water like clarified butter trickling down from it.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْمَلِكُ لَابِسَ كُفُوفٍ مِنْ جِلْدِ السُّرَادِقِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-maliku lābisa kufūfin min jildi al-surādiqi
sentences.l: And the king was wearing gloves of the leather of the pavilion-tent.
sentences.i: Now the king was wearing gloves made of tent-leather,

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الطَّاسَةَ مِنْ رَقَبَةِ الْبَازِ وَمَلَأَهَا مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْمَاءِ وَوَضَعَ الْمَاءَ قُدَّامَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-ṭāsata min raqabati al-bāzi wa-malaʾahā min dhālika al-māʾi wa-waḍaʿa al-māʾa quddāmahu
sentences.l: so he took the cup from the falcon's neck, and filled it from that water, and set the water before him.
sentences.i: so he took the cup from the falcon's neck, filled it with that water, and set it down before him.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْبَازِ لَطَسَ الطَّاسَةَ قَلَبَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-bāzi laṭasa al-ṭāsata qalabahā
sentences.l: And behold, the falcon struck the cup — knocked it over.
sentences.i: And all at once the falcon knocked the cup and overturned it.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الطَّاسَةَ ثَانِيًا وَأَخَذَ النَّفْطَ النَّازِلَةَ حَتَّى مَلَأَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-ṭāsata thāniyan wa-akhadha al-nafṭa al-nāzilata ḥattā malaʾahā
sentences.l: So he took the cup a second time, and took the dripping naphtha [-like liquid] until he had filled it,
sentences.i: So he took up the cup a second time and caught the oily liquid dripping down until he had filled it,
sentences.n: النَّفْط ('naphtha, oil') is printed with ف rather than ق; given that النَّازِلَة agreeing with it is feminine while نفط is ordinarily masculine, this may be a misprint for النُّقْطَة, 'the drop' (ف/ق are easily confused), which would also better match the feminine adjective. It is vocalized and translated as printed, with this uncertainty flagged rather than silently corrected; either way the sense — the oily-looking liquid dripping from the tree, described earlier as being like clarified butter — is the same.

sentences.t: وَظَنَّ أَنَّ الْبَازَ عَطْشَانُ فَوَضَعَهَا قُدَّامَهُ فَلَطَسَهَا قَلَبَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ẓanna anna al-bāza ʿaṭshānu fa-waḍaʿahā quddāmahu fa-laṭasahā qalabahā
sentences.l: and he supposed that the falcon was thirsty; so he set it before it, and it struck it — overturned it.
sentences.i: supposing the falcon must be thirsty; but when he set it down before the bird, it knocked it over again.

sentences.t: فَانْقَبَضَ الْمَلِكُ مِنَ الْبَازِ
sentences.tr: fa-inqabaḍa al-maliku mina al-bāzi
sentences.l: So the king was vexed at the falcon.
sentences.i: At this the king grew vexed with the falcon.
sentences.n: اِنْقَبَضَ (Form VII of قَبَضَ) is used here in the idiomatic sense of feeling constrained, annoyed, or put out — not its literal sense of physical contraction.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ ثَالِثَ مَرَّةٍ وَمَلَاءَ الطَّاسَةَ وَقَدَّمَهَا لِلْحِصَانِ فَقَلَبَهَا الْبَازُ بِجَنَاحِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma thālitha marratin wa-malāʾa al-ṭāsata wa-qaddamahā lil-ḥiṣāni fa-qalabahā al-bāzu bi-janāḥihi
sentences.l: And he rose a third time, and filled the cup, and offered it to the horse; and the falcon overturned it with its wing.
sentences.i: He got up a third time, filled the cup, and offered it to the horse instead — but the falcon overturned that too, with a sweep of its wing.
sentences.n: وَمَلَاءَ spells 'he filled' with the hamza written bare after an extra long alif (compare فَطَاطَاءَ above), rather than the more usual مَلَأَ seen twice earlier in this same passage — the same verb inconsistently spelled within a few lines, a genuine feature of the print kept as given.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ اللَّهُ يُشَيِّبُكَ يَا أَيْشَمَ الطُّيُورِ أَحْرَمْتَنِي مِنَ الشُّرْبِ وَأَحْرَمْتَ نَفْسَكَ وَأَحْرَمْتَ الْحِصَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku Allāhu yushayyibuka yā ayshama al-ṭuyūri aḥramtanī mina al-shurbi wa-aḥramta nafsaka wa-aḥramta al-ḥiṣāna
sentences.l: So the king said: 'God age you, O most ill-omened of birds! You have deprived me of drinking, and deprived yourself, and deprived the horse.'
sentences.i: At this the king cried, 'God grey your head, most ill-omened of birds! You have robbed me of my drink, and robbed yourself, and robbed the horse besides!'
sentences.n: اللَّهُ يُشَيِّبُكَ ('may God make you grey-haired') is an imprecation — roughly 'may this age you with grief', i.e. 'damn you.' أَيْشَمَ stands for أَشْأَم, the elative 'most ill-omened' (from شُؤْم); its ي replaces the expected medial hamza, the same colloquial hamza-weakening already seen in نَايِمَة for نَائِمَة.

sentences.t: وَضَرَبَ الْبَازَ بِالسَّيْفِ رَمَى أَجْنِحَتَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ḍaraba al-bāza bi-al-sayfi ramā ajniḥatahu
sentences.l: And he struck the falcon with the sword — cast off its wings.
sentences.i: And with that he struck the falcon with his sword, shearing off its wings.

sentences.t: فَصَارَ الطَّيْرُ يُقِيمُ رَأْسَهُ وَيَقُولُ بِالْإِشَارَةِ انْظُرْ الَّذِي فَوْقَ الشَّجَرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāra al-ṭayru yuqīmu raʾsahu wa-yaqūlu bi-al-ishārati unẓur alladhī fawqa al-shajarati
sentences.l: Then the bird began to raise its head, and to say by gesture: 'Look at that which is above the tree.'
sentences.i: Then the bird began lifting its head, signaling as if to say, 'Look at what is above the tree!'

sentences.t: فَقَامَ الْمَلِكُ عَيْنَهُ فَرَأَى فَوْقَ الشَّجَرَةِ فَرْخَ آفَةٍ وَهَذَا سَمُّهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma al-maliku ʿaynahu fa-raʾā fawqa al-shajarati farkha āfatin wa-hādhā sammuhā
sentences.l: So the king raised his eye, and saw above the tree the young of a viper — and this was its venom.
sentences.i: So the king lifted his gaze, and there above the tree he saw a young viper — and it was its venom that had been dripping down.
sentences.n: قَامَ عَيْنَهُ ('he raised his eye') uses قَامَ transitively, an unusual extension of a normally intransitive verb (Classically one would expect a Form IV أَقَامَ); rendered by sense. آفَة, generically 'a pest, a blight', is used here concretely for a venomous snake.

sentences.t: فَنَدِمَ الْمَلِكُ عَلَى قَصِّ أَجْنِحَةِ الْبَازِ
sentences.tr: fa-nadima al-maliku ʿalā qaṣṣi ajniḥati al-bāzi
sentences.l: So the king regretted the cutting of the wings of the falcon.
sentences.i: And the king was overcome with regret at having clipped the falcon's wings.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ وَرَكِبَ حِصَانَهُ وَسَارَ وَمَعَهُ الْغَزَالَةُ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى الْوَطَاقِ بِمَتَاعِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma wa-rakiba ḥiṣānahu wa-sāra wa-maʿahu al-ghazālatu ilā an waṣala ilā al-waṭāqi bi-matāʿihi
sentences.l: And he rose, and mounted his horse, and set out, and with him [was] the gazelle, until he arrived at the camp with his gear.
sentences.i: He rose, mounted his horse, and rode back with the gazelle, until he reached the camp with the rest of his gear,

sentences.t: فَأَعْطَى الْغَزَالَةَ إِلَى الطَّبَّاخِ وَقَالَ لَهُ خُذْ شَوِّهَا
sentences.tr: fa-aʿṭā al-ghazālata ilā al-ṭabbākhi wa-qāla lahu khudh shawwihā
sentences.l: and he gave the gazelle to the cook, and said to him: 'Take it — roast it.'
sentences.i: and gave the gazelle to the cook, telling him, 'Here, roast this.'

sentences.t: وَجَلَسَ الْمَلِكُ عَلَى الْكُرْسِيِّ وَالْبَازُ عَلَى يَدِهِ فَتَحَقَّقَ الْبَازُ مَاتَ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasa al-maliku ʿalā al-kursiyyi wa-al-bāzu ʿalā yadihi fa-taḥaqqaqa al-bāzu māta
sentences.l: And the king sat upon the chair, and the falcon upon his hand; then it became certain — the falcon had died.
sentences.i: The king sat down upon his chair with the falcon still on his hand — and then it became plain: the falcon was dead.
sentences.n: فَتَحَقَّقَ الْبَازُ مَاتَ juxtaposes two clauses without a connective ('it became certain, the falcon died'), a paratactic Middle Arabic construction for 'it became certain that the falcon had died.'

sentences.t: فَصَرَخَ الْمَلِكُ حُزْنًا وَأَسَفًا عَلَى قَتْلِ الْبَازِ وَكَوْنِهِ خَلَّصَهُ مِنَ الْهَلَاكِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣarakha al-maliku ḥuznan wa-asafan ʿalā qatli al-bāzi wa-kawnihi khallaṣahu mina al-halāki
sentences.l: So the king cried out in grief and sorrow over the killing of the falcon, and its having freed him from destruction.
sentences.i: And the king cried out in grief and sorrow, mourning the falcon he had killed — the very falcon that had saved him from destruction.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ حَدِيثِ الْمَلِكِ السِّنْدِبَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā mā kāna min ḥadīthi al-maliki al-Sindibādi
sentences.l: And this is what was of the story of King al-Sindibad.
sentences.i: So much, then, for the story of King al-Sindibad.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ كَلَامَ الْمَلِكِ يُونَانَ قَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ الْعَظِيمُ الشَّأْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru kalāma al-maliki Yūnāna qāla lahu ayyuhā al-maliku al-ʿaẓīmu al-shaʾni
sentences.l: So when the vizier heard King Yunan's words, he said to him, 'O king, great of rank,'
sentences.i: When the vizier heard King Yunan's words, he said to him, 'O king of exalted rank,'
sentences.n: الشَّأْنِ preserves the classical idiom عَظِيمُ الشَّأْنِ ('great of rank/dignity'), a stock honorific with الشأن as the mudāf ilayh; the edition prints its hamza-seat alif bare, so a combining hamza is supplied here rather than the precomposed letter.

sentences.t: وَمَا الَّذِي فِعْلُهُ مِنَ الضَّرُورَةِ وَلَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْهُ سُوْءًا
sentences.tr: wa-mā alladhī fiʿluhu mina al-ḍarūrati wa-lā raʾaytu minhu sūʾan
sentences.l: There is nothing that his deed is of necessity, nor have I seen from him [any] evil,
sentences.i: there was no necessity behind what he has done, nor have I myself seen any wrong in him,
sentences.n: The referent of 'his' (in فِعْلُهُ and مِنْهُ) is left ambiguous on the page — it could point back to Duban, the subject under discussion, or loosely to the king's own conduct in defending him; translated on the assumption that it is Duban, which best fits the vizier's climb-down after the king's rebuke.

sentences.t: وَإِنَّمَا أَفْعَلُ هَذَا شَفَقَةً عَلَيْكَ وَلِأَجْلِ أَنْ تَعْلَمَ صِحَّةَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-innamā afʿalu hādhā shafaqatan ʿalayka wa-li-ajli an taʿlama ṣiḥḥata dhālika
sentences.l: I only do this out of pity for you, and for the sake of your knowing the soundness of that,
sentences.i: I do this only out of concern for you, so that you may be certain of the truth of the matter,

sentences.t: وَإِلَّا هَلَكْتَ كَمَا هَلَكَ وَزِيرٌ كَانَ اِحْتَالَ عَلَى اِبْنِ مَلِكٍ مِنَ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: wa-illā halakta kamā halaka wazīrun kāna iḥtāla ʿalā ibni malikin mina al-mulūki
sentences.l: or else you will perish, as a vizier perished who had schemed against a son of a king, among the kings.
sentences.i: or else you may come to grief, as a vizier once perished who had plotted against a king's son.
sentences.n: كَانَ اِحْتَالَ (kāna + past) forms a pluperfect, 'had schemed' — setting up the embedded cautionary tale that follows.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْمَلِكُ يُونَانُ وَكَيْفَ كَانَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla al-maliku Yūnānu wa-kayfa kāna dhālika
sentences.l: King Yunan said, 'And how was that?'

sentences.t: حِكَايَةُ الْوَزِيرِ الْمُحْتَالِ
sentences.tr: ḥikāyatu al-wazīri al-muḥtāli
sentences.l: The Story of the Scheming Vizier
sentences.n: A section heading the edition prints as its own line, opening the vizier's embedded tale-within-the-tale (compare the parallel heading in nights-04). الْمُحْتَالِ is the form-VIII active participle of اِحْتَالَ, 'one who schemes/uses a stratagem.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ اِعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ وَزِيرًا كَانَ لِبَعْضِ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku anna wazīran kāna li-baʿḍi al-mulūki
sentences.l: The vizier said, 'Know, O king, that a vizier belonged to one of the kings,'
sentences.i: The vizier said, 'Know, O king, that there once was a vizier in the service of one of the kings,'

sentences.t: وَكَانَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ مُولَعٌ بِالصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna lahu waladun mūlaʿun bi-al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi
sentences.l: and he had a son devoted to hunting and the chase.
sentences.i: who had a son passionately fond of hunting and the chase.
sentences.n: مُولَعٌ, the form-IV passive participle of وَلِعَ, 'to be devoted/addicted to.'

sentences.t: وَكَانَ مَعَهُ وَزِيرٌ لِأَبِيهِ قَدْ أَمَرَهُ أَبُوهُ الْمَلِكُ أَنْ يَكُونَ مَعَهُ أَيْنَمَا تَوَجَّهَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna maʿahu wazīrun li-abīhi qad amarahu abūhu al-maliku an yakūna maʿahu aynamā tawajjaha
sentences.l: And with him was a vizier of his father's; his father the king had commanded him to be with him wherever he set out.
sentences.i: He was accompanied by a vizier of his father's, whom the king his father had ordered to stay with him wherever he went.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ كَانَ يَوْمًا مِنْ بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ خَرَجَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ وَخَرَجَ مَعَهُ وَزِيرُ أَبِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad kāna yawman min baʿḍi al-ayyāmi kharaja al-waladu ilā al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi wa-kharaja maʿahu wazīru abīhi
sentences.l: And it was, one day among the days, that the boy went out to hunting and the chase, and his father's vizier went out with him,
sentences.i: Now one day the boy set out to hunt and course game, and his father's vizier went out with him,
sentences.n: يَوْمًا مِنْ بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ, 'one day among the days,' is the tale's stock formula for a narrative beginning.

sentences.t: فَسَارُوا جَمِيعًا فَنَظَرُوا إِلَى وَحْشِيٍّ كَبِيرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-sārū jamīʿan fa-naẓarū ilā waḥshiyyin kabīrin
sentences.l: and they journeyed together, and they caught sight of a great wild beast.
sentences.i: and they rode on together until they caught sight of a great wild beast.
sentences.n: وَحْشِيّ, properly the nisba adjective 'wild,' is used here substantively for 'a wild beast/animal,' a Middle Arabic usage.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ لِاِبْنِ الْمَلِكِ دُونَكَ هَذَا الْوَحْشِيَّ فَاُطْلُبْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru li-ibni al-maliki dūnaka hādhā al-waḥshiyya fa-uṭlubhu
sentences.l: The vizier said to the prince, 'Here is this wild beast for you — pursue it!'
sentences.i: The vizier said to the prince, 'There is your quarry — after it!'
sentences.n: دُونَكَ is the presentative exclamation ('here, take...'), regularly followed by an imperative, as here.

sentences.t: فَقَصَدَ اِبْنُ الْمَلِكِ حَتَّى غَابَ عَنِ الْعَيْنِ وَغَابَ عَنْهُ الْوَحْشِيُّ فِي الْبَرِّيَّةِ لَا يَعْرِفُ أَيْنَ يَرُوحُ وَلَا أَيْنَ يَسِيرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qaṣada ibnu al-maliki ḥattā ghāba ʿani al-ʿayni wa-ghāba ʿanhu al-waḥshiyyu fī al-barriyyati lā yaʿrifu ayna yarūḥu wa-lā ayna yasīru
sentences.l: So the prince made for it until he vanished from sight, and the beast vanished from him in the wilderness — he did not know where to go nor where to travel.
sentences.i: So the prince rode after it until he passed out of sight, and the beast vanished from him in the wilderness, leaving him not knowing which way to turn.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِجَارِيَةٍ عَلَى رَأْسِ الطَّرِيقِ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-jāriyatin ʿalā raʾsi al-ṭarīqi wa-hiya tabkī
sentences.l: And then, [there was] a girl at the head of the road, weeping.
sentences.i: And then, there at the roadside was a girl, weeping.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِـ is the 'surprise' construction seen already in nights-04 (وَإِذَا بِالصَّيَّادِ).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا اِبْنُ الْمَلِكِ مَنْ أَنْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā ibnu al-maliki man anti
sentences.l: The prince said to her, 'Who are you?'

sentences.t: قَالَتْ أَنَا بِنْتُ مَلِكٍ مِنْ مُلُوكِ الْهِنْدِ وَكُنْتُ فِي الْبَرِّيَّةِ فَأَدْرَكَنِي النُّعَاسُ فَوَقَعْتُ مِنْ عَلَى الدَّابَّةِ وَلَمْ أَعْلَمْ بِنَفْسِي فَصِرْتُ مُنْقَطِعَةً حَائِرَةً
sentences.tr: qālat anā bintu malikin min mulūki al-hindi wa-kuntu fī al-barriyyati fa-adrakanī al-nuʿāsu fa-waqaʿtu min ʿalā al-dābbati wa-lam aʿlam bi-nafsī fa-ṣirtu munqaṭiʿatan ḥāʾiratan
sentences.l: She said, 'I am the daughter of a king among the kings of India; I was in the wilderness, and drowsiness overtook me, and I fell from off the mount, and I did not know of myself; so I became cut off [and] bewildered.'
sentences.i: She said, 'I am the daughter of a king of India. I was crossing the wilderness when drowsiness overcame me, and I fell from my mount without even knowing it — and so I was left stranded and bewildered.'
sentences.n: مُنْقَطِعَة, lit. 'cut off,' i.e. stranded, separated from her party.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ اِبْنُ الْمَلِكِ كَلَامَهَا رَثَى لِحَالِهَا وَحَمَلَهَا عَلَى ظَهْرِ دَابَّتِهِ وَأَرْدَفَهَا وَسَارَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa ibnu al-maliki kalāmahā rathā li-ḥālihā wa-ḥamalahā ʿalā ẓahri dābbatihi wa-ardafahā wa-sāra
sentences.l: So when the prince heard her words he pitied her state, and carried her upon the back of his mount and set her behind him, and journeyed on.
sentences.i: When the prince heard her story he took pity on her plight; he lifted her onto the back of his mount, seated her behind him, and rode on.
sentences.n: أَرْدَفَهَا, form IV of رَدِفَ, 'to seat someone behind oneself [on a mount].'

sentences.t: حَتَّى مَرَّ بِخَرَابَةٍ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْجَارِيَةُ يَا سَيِّدِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُزِيلَ ضَرُورَةً
sentences.tr: ḥattā marra bi-kharābatin fa-qālat lahu al-jāriyatu yā sayyidī urīdu an uzīla ḍarūratan
sentences.l: until he passed by a ruin, and the girl said to him, 'O my master, I want to remove a necessity.'
sentences.i: until he passed by some ruins, and the girl said to him, 'My lord, I must relieve myself.'
sentences.n: أُزِيلَ ضَرُورَةً, lit. 'that I remove a pressing need,' is the text's euphemism for relieving oneself; kept literal here alongside the plain idiomatic sense.

sentences.t: فَأَنْزَلَهَا إِلَى الْخَرَابَةِ فَعَوَّقَتْ فَاِسْتَبْطَأَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-anzalahā ilā al-kharābati fa-ʿawwaqat fa-istabṭaʾahā
sentences.l: So he set her down at the ruin, and she delayed herself, and he found her tarrying too long.
sentences.i: So he set her down among the ruins; but she lingered, and he grew impatient waiting for her.
sentences.n: عَوَّقَتْ (form II, 'she held herself up/delayed') and اِسْتَبْطَأَهَا (form X, 'he deemed her slow') are both derived from the notion of delay.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ خَلْفَهَا وَهُوَ لَا يَعْلَمُ بِهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ غُولَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala khalfahā wa-huwa lā yaʿlamu bihā fa-idhā hiya ghūlatun
sentences.l: So he went in after her, while he did not know about her, and then — she was a ghouleh!
sentences.i: So he went in after her, unaware of what she truly was — and there she was, a ghouleh!
sentences.n: غُولَة (ghouleh), a female man-eating desert demon, is printed and kept as the edition spells it throughout this passage.

sentences.t: وَهِيَ تَقُولُ لِأَوْلَادِهَا يَا أَوْلَادِي قَدْ أَتَيْتُكُمُ الْيَوْمَ بِغُلَامٍ سَمِينٍ
sentences.tr: wa-hiya taqūlu li-awlādihā yā awlādī qad ataytukumu al-yawma bi-ghulāmin samīnin
sentences.l: and she was saying to her children, 'O my children, I have brought you today a fat boy.'
sentences.i: and she was saying to her children, 'My children, today I have brought you a plump boy.'

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهَا اِئْتِينَا بِهِ يَا أُمَّنَا حَتَّى نَرْعَاهُ فِي بُطُونِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahā iʾtīnā bihi yā ummanā ḥattā narʿāhu fī buṭūninā
sentences.l: They said to her, 'Bring him to us, O our mother, so that we may graze on him in our bellies.'
sentences.i: They said to her, 'Bring him to us, mother, so we can feast on him in our bellies!'
sentences.n: اِئْتِينَا: feminine-singular imperative of أَتَى ('to bring, lit. come with') plus the object suffix -نا, addressed by the plural children to their single mother — not the more expected ائتونا, but this is what the rasm ايتينا (identical letter-count) supports. The cannibal image is translated plainly, per house policy against bowdlerizing.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ اِبْنُ الْمَلِكِ كَلَامَهُمْ أَيْقَنَ بِالْهَلَاكِ وَارْتَعَدَتْ فَرَائِصُهُ وَخَشِيَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَرَجَعَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa ibnu al-maliki kalāmahum ayqana bi-al-halāki wa-irtaʿadat farāʾiṣuhu wa-khashiya ʿalā nafsihi wa-rajaʿa
sentences.l: So when the prince heard their words he became certain of destruction, and his flanks trembled, and he feared for himself, and he turned back.
sentences.i: When the prince heard them speak he knew for certain he was doomed; his whole body shook with terror, and fearing for his life, he turned back.
sentences.n: فَرَائِصُهُ, pl. of فَرِيصَة, the flank-muscle proverbially said to quiver with fear — idiomatic for 'his flesh crawled with terror.'

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتِ الْغُولَةُ فَرَأَتْهُ كَالْخَائِفِ الْوَجِلِ وَ هُوَ يَرْتَعِدُ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajati al-ghūlatu fa-raʾathu ka-al-khāʾifi al-wajili wa-huwa yartaʿidu
sentences.l: Then the ghouleh came out and saw him like the fearful, the terrified — trembling.
sentences.i: Then the ghouleh came out and found him fearful and terror-stricken, trembling all over.
sentences.n: كَالْخَائِفِ الْوَجِلِ pairs two near-synonyms for 'afraid' for emphasis.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ مَا بَالُكَ خَائِفٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu mā bāluka khāʾifun
sentences.l: She said to him, 'What is your state — [are you] afraid?'
sentences.i: She said to him, 'What ails you, that you are so afraid?'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنَّ لِي عَدُوًّا وَأَنَا خَائِفٌ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla inna lī ʿaduwwan wa-anā khāʾifun minhu
sentences.l: He said, 'I have an enemy, and I am afraid of him.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْغُولَةُ إِنَّكَ تَقُولُ أَنَا اِبْنُ مَلِكٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ghūlatu innaka taqūlu anā ibnu malikin
sentences.l: The ghouleh said, 'You say, I am a king's son.'
sentences.i: The ghouleh said, 'But you say you are a king's son.'
sentences.n: The quoted claim (أَنَا ابْنُ مَلِكٍ) follows إِنَّكَ تَقُولُ with no reporting particle, the loosely paratactic direct-quotation style seen throughout this register.

sentences.t: قَٰلَ لَهَا نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: qāla lahā naʿam
sentences.l: He said to her, 'Yes.'
sentences.n: قل is the edition's defective spelling of قال, pointed here with the dagger alif (ٰ) per house convention: it preserves the rasm exactly and strips back to it.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ مَا لَكَ لَا تَدْفَعُ لِعَدُوِّكَ شَيًا مِنَ الْمَالِ تُرْضِيهِ بِهِ
sentences.tr: qālat lahu mā laka lā tadfaʿu li-ʿaduwwika shayan mina al-māli turḍīhi bihi
sentences.l: She said to him, 'What is [wrong] with you, that you do not give to your enemy something of [your] wealth to satisfy him with?'
sentences.i: She said to him, 'Why do you not give your enemy something of your wealth to appease him?'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا إِنَّهُ لَا يَرْضَى بِمَالٍ إِلَّا بِالرُّوحِ وَأَنَا خَائِفٌ مِنْهُ وَ أَنَا رَجُلٌ مَظْلُومٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā innahu lā yarḍā bi-mālin illā bi-al-rūḥi wa-anā khāʾifun minhu wa-anā rajulun maẓlūmun
sentences.l: He said to her, 'He will not be satisfied with wealth — only with [my] life — and I am afraid of him, and I am a wronged man.'
sentences.i: He replied, 'Nothing will content him but my life — no wealth will do — and I am afraid of him, for I am a man who has been wronged.'
sentences.n: بِالرُّوحِ, 'with the soul/life,' i.e. nothing short of his death will satisfy the enemy.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنْ كُنْتَ مَظْلُومًا لِمَا تَزْعُمُ اِسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ فَإِنَّهُ يَكْفِيكَ شَرَّهُ وَ شَرَّ مَا تَخَافُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu in kunta maẓlūman li-mā tazʿumu istaʿin bi-Allāhi fa-innahu yakfīka sharrahu wa-sharra mā takhāfu minhu
sentences.l: She said to him, 'If you are wronged, as you claim, seek help in God, for He will suffice you [against] his evil and the evil of what you fear from him.'
sentences.i: She said to him, 'If you are indeed wronged, as you say, then seek help from God, for He will spare you his harm and the harm of whatever you fear.'

sentences.t: فَرَفَعَ اِبْنُ الْمَلِكِ رَأْسَهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَ قَالَ يَا مَنْ يُجِيبُ الْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَ يَكْشِفُ السُّوءَ
sentences.tr: fa-rafaʿa ibnu al-maliki raʾsahu ilā al-samāʾi wa-qāla yā man yujību al-muḍṭarra idhā daʿāhu wa-yakshifu al-sūʾa
sentences.l: So the prince raised his head to the sky and said, 'O You who answer the distressed one when he calls upon You, and remove the evil,'
sentences.i: So the prince raised his head to heaven and cried, 'O You who answer the one in distress when he calls upon You, and who lift away harm —'
sentences.n: This echoes Qur'an 27:62 (أَمَّنْ يُجِيبُ الْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ السُّوءَ); the prayer borrows the Qur'anic phrasing without the interrogative أَمَّنْ of the verse itself.

sentences.t: اللَّهُمَّ اُنْصُرْنِي عَلَى عَدُوِّي وَ اِصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي إِنَّكَ عَلَى مَا تَشَاءُ قَدِيرٌ
sentences.tr: Allāhumma unṣurnī ʿalā ʿaduwwī wa-iṣrifhu ʿannī innaka ʿalā mā tashāʾu qadīrun
sentences.l: 'O God, help me against my enemy, and turn him away from me; verily You are, over what You will, able.'
sentences.i: 'O God, grant me victory over my enemy, and turn him away from me — surely You have power over all that You will.'

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الْغُولَةُ دُعَاءَهُ انْصَرَفَتْ عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-ghūlatu duʿāʾahu inṣarafat ʿanhu
sentences.l: So when the ghouleh heard his prayer, she turned away from him.

sentences.t: وَ انْصَرَفَ اِبْنُ الْمَلِكِ إِلَى أَبِيهِ وَ حَدَّثَهُ بِحَدِيثِ الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: wa-inṣarafa ibnu al-maliki ilā abīhi wa-ḥaddathahu bi-ḥadīthi al-wazīri
sentences.l: And the prince turned back to his father, and told him the story of the vizier.
sentences.i: And the prince went back to his father and told him what the vizier had done.

sentences.t: فَأَدْعَى الْمَلِكُ بِالْوَزِيرِ وَ قَتَلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-adʿā al-maliku bi-al-wazīri wa-qatalahu
sentences.l: So the king called for the vizier, and killed him.
sentences.i: At that, the king sent for the vizier and put him to death.
sentences.n: أَدْعَى spells دَعَا بِـ ('to send/call for') with an extra prosthetic initial hamza, giving it the shape of a form-IV verb while keeping the plain form-I sense — the same phenomenon nights-04 notes for أَخْلَعَ standing in for خَلَعَ.

sentences.t: وَ أَنْتَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ مَتَى أَمِنْتَ لِهَذَا الْحَكِيمِ
sentences.tr: wa-anta ayyuhā al-maliku matā aminta li-hādhā al-ḥakīm
sentences.l: And you, O King, when have you trusted this sage?
sentences.i: And you, O King — since when have you placed your trust in this sage?

sentences.t: قَتْلُكَ شَرُّ الْقَتَلَاتِ الَّذِي قَدْ أَحْسَنْتَ إِلَيْهِ وَ قَرَّبْتَهُ مِنْكَ يَعْمَلُ عَلَى هَلَاكِكَ
sentences.tr: qatluka sharru al-qatalāti alladhī qad aḥsanta ilayhi wa-qarrabtahu minka yaʿmalu ʿalā halākika
sentences.l: Your death would be the worst of deaths: he to whom you have done good and whom you have drawn near to you works toward your destruction.
sentences.i: Your death at his hands would be the worst of deaths: the very man you have shown kindness and drawn close to you is working toward your ruin.
sentences.n: قَتَلَات is the plural of qatla, 'a killing, a manner of dying' — a rhetorical intensifier ('the worst of the ways of being killed'), not a literal plural of separate murders. الَّذِي picks up a distant antecedent — the sage of the previous sentence — rather than one immediately before it, a loose, paratactic habit typical of this narrative style.

sentences.t: أَمَا تَرَى أَنَّهُ أَبْرَأَكَ مِنَ الْمَرَضِ مِنْ ظَاهِرِ الْجَسَدِ بِشَيْءٍ مَسَكْتَهُ بِيَدِكَ
sentences.tr: amā tarā annahu abraʾaka mina al-maraḍi min ẓāhiri al-jasadi bi-shayʾin masaktahu bi-yadika
sentences.l: Do you not see that he cured you of the disease, from the outside of the body, with a thing you held in your hand?
sentences.i: Do you not see that he cured you of your disease — from the surface of the body — by means of a thing you held in your hand?
sentences.n: مِنْ ظَاهِرِ الْجَسَدِ, 'from the outward part of the body', specifies that the cure worked through the skin, by touch — the detail the vizier's whole argument turns on, to make sudden death by touch (and, in a moment, by smell) seem credible.

sentences.t: فَلَا تَأْمَنْ أَنْ يُهْلِكَكَ بِشَيْءٍ تَمْسِكُهُ أَيْضًا
sentences.tr: fa-lā taʾman an yuhlikaka bi-shayʾin tamsikuhu ayḍan
sentences.l: So do not feel safe that he might destroy you with another thing you would hold.
sentences.i: So do not feel secure that he might not destroy you likewise, with some other thing you touch.
sentences.n: The vizier's own words here are bi-shayʾin tamsikuhu, 'with something you hold' (by hand); a few lines on, the king recasts the danger as bi-shayʾin ashummuhu, 'with something I smell' — the text itself shifts the imagined means of poisoning between the two speeches, kept here exactly as printed rather than harmonized.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ يُونَانُ صَدَقْتَ يَا وَزِيرُ وَ قَدْ يَكُونُ كَمَا ذَكَرْتَ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ النَّاصِحُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku Yūnānu ṣadaqta yā wazīru wa-qad yakūnu kamā dhakarta ayyuhā al-wazīru al-nāṣiḥu
sentences.l: So King Yunan said: You have spoken truly, O vizier; and it may well be as you have said, O sincere vizier.
sentences.i: King Yunan said: You have spoken the truth, vizier; it may indeed be as you say, O faithful vizier.

sentences.t: وَ إِنَّ هَذَا الْحَكِيمَ أَتَى جَاسُوسًا فِي طَلَبِ هَلَاكِي وَ إِنْ يَكُنْ أَبْرَأَنِي بِشَيْءٍ مَسَكْتُهُ بِيَدِي يَقْدِرُ أَنْ يُهْلِكَنِي بِشَيْءٍ أَشُمُّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-inna hādhā al-ḥakīma atā jāsūsan fī ṭalabi halākī wa-in yakun abraʾanī bi-shayʾin masaktuhu bi-yadī yaqdiru an yuhlikanī bi-shayʾin ashummuhu
sentences.l: And indeed this sage has come as a spy in pursuit of my destruction; and even if he cured me with a thing I held in my hand, he is able to destroy me with a thing I smell.
sentences.i: This sage, indeed, has come as a spy seeking my death; and even though he cured me with something I held in my hand, he is capable of killing me with something I merely smell.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ يُونَانَ قَٰلَ لِوَزِيرِهِ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ كَيْفَ الْعَمَلُ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika Yūnāna qāla li-wazīrihi ayyuhā al-wazīru kayfa al-ʿamalu fīhi
sentences.l: Then King Yunan said to his vizier: O vizier, what is to be done about him?
sentences.i: Then King Yunan said to his vizier: O vizier, how are we to deal with him?
sentences.n: The edition prints قل here without the alif of qāla, as it does throughout; it is pointed with a dagger alif (قَٰلَ) so that the printed consonants stand exactly as given while the word still reads qāla, matching the convention already established for this same spelling elsewhere.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ أَرْسِلْ خَلْفَهُ فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ وَ اطْلُبْهُ فَإِنْ حَضَرَ فَاضْرِبْ عُنُقَهُ فَتَكْفِي شَرَّهُ وَ تَسْتَرِيحُ مِنْهُ وَ اغْدِرْ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَغْدِرَ بِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru arsil khalfahu fī hādhā al-waqti wa-uṭlubhu fa-in ḥaḍara fa-iḍrib ʿunuqahu fa-takfī sharrahu wa-tastarīḥu minhu wa-ighdir bihi qabla an yaghdira bika
sentences.l: So the vizier said to him: Send after him at this time and summon him; if he comes, strike off his neck, and so you will be rid of his mischief and be at ease from him; betray him before he betrays you.
sentences.i: The vizier said to him: Send for him at once and have him brought; and if he comes, strike off his head — thus you will be quit of his mischief and set your mind at rest concerning him. Betray him before he can betray you.
sentences.n: اغدر به قبل أن يغدر بك, 'betray him before he betrays you', turns the very lesson of the vizier's own cautionary tale — treachery answered with treachery — into direct counsel; the root غدر runs through this whole frame-tale sequence.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ يُونَانُ صَدَقْتَ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku Yūnānu ṣadaqta ayyuhā al-wazīru
sentences.l: So King Yunan said: You have spoken truly, O vizier.
sentences.i: King Yunan said: You have spoken truly, O vizier.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَرْسَلَ إِلَى الْحَكِيمِ فَحَضَرَ وَ هُوَ فَرْحَانُ وَ لَا يَعْلَمُ مَا قَدَّرَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ كَمَا قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ فِي الْمَعْنَى
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika arsala ilā al-ḥakīmi fa-ḥaḍara wa-huwa farḥānu wa-lā yaʿlamu mā qaddarahu al-raḥmānu kamā qāla baʿḍuhum fī al-maʿnā
sentences.l: Then the king sent for the sage, and he came, joyful, not knowing what the All-Merciful had decreed for him — as someone has said, to this effect:
sentences.i: Then the king sent for the sage, and he came, rejoicing, unaware of what the All-Merciful had ordained for him — as someone has said, to this effect:
sentences.n: بَعْضُهُمْ فِي الْمَعْنَى, 'someone [has said], to this effect', is the narrator's own formula for introducing the gnomic verse that follows and those like it later in this passage — it is not spoken by any character on stage, but is the storyteller's aside to the audience.

sentences.t: اِنَّ الْبَقَاءَ كَائِنٌ يَا سَيِّدِي * فَلَكَ الْاَمَانُ مِنَ الَّذِي مَا قَدَرَا
sentences.tr: inna al-baqāʾa kāʾinun yā sayyidī * fa-laka al-amānu mina al-ladhī mā qadarā
sentences.l: Indeed, permanence is a real thing, O my lord; so you have safety from that which was not decreed.
sentences.i: Continuance in this world is a real and certain thing, my lord; you are safe from all but what has been ordained for you.
sentences.n: This single couplet is the narrator's own aside, addressed to no one on stage — a proverbial reflection on fate slipped in just before Duban walks in unaware of his danger. الْاَمَان and قَدَرَا are printed by the edition without a hamza mark, as elsewhere in its verse; قَدَرَا carries the pausal spelling with final alif rather than tanwīn, for the rhyme.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ الْحَكِيمُ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ أَنْشَدَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala al-ḥakīmu ʿalā al-maliki anshada
sentences.l: And when the sage came in to the king, he recited:
sentences.i: And when the sage entered before the king, he recited:

sentences.t:
اِذَا لَمْ اَتِمَّ فِي بَعْضِ ذَلِكَ بِالشُّكْرِ * فَعَلَ لِي لِمَنْ اَعْدَدْتُ نَظْمِي اَوْ نَثْرِي
لَعَلَّ جُدْتَ لِي قَبْلَ السُّؤَالِ بِانْعُمِ * اَتَيَقَّنُ بِلَا مَطْلٍ لَدَيْكَ وَلَا عُذْرِ
فَمَا لِي لَا اُعْطِي ثَنَاءَكَ حَقَّهُ * وَاِنَّنِي عَلَى جَدْوَاكَ فِي السِّرِّ وَالجَهْرِ
سَاَذْكُرُ مَا اَوْلَيْتَنِي مِنْ صَنَائِعٍ * يَخِفُّ بِهَا دَيْنِي وَاِنْ اَطَالَتْ ظَهْرِي
sentences.tr:
idhā lam atimma fī baʿḍi dhālika bi-al-shukri * faʿala lī li-man aʿdadtu naẓmī aw nathrī
laʿalla judta lī qabla al-suʾāli bi-anʿumi * atayaqqanu bi-lā maṭlin ladayka wa-lā ʿudhri
fa-mā lī lā uʿṭī thanāʾaka ḥaqqahu * wa-innanī ʿalā jadwāka fī al-sirri wa-al-jahri
sa-adhkuru mā awlaytanī min ṣanāʾiʿin * yakhiffu bihā daynī wa-in aṭālat ẓahrī
sentences.l:
If I do not fulfill, for some part of that, with thanks, what he has done for me — he for whom I have prepared my verse or my prose —
perhaps you were generous to me, before the asking, with favors; of this I am certain, with no delay from you and no excuse.
What excuse, then, have I not to give your praise its due, when I bear witness to your bounty in secret and in open?
I shall recount the kindnesses you have granted me — kindnesses by which my debt grows light, though they have burdened my back.
sentences.i:
If for some part of what he has done for me I should fail to render full thanks — he for whom I have made ready my verse and my prose —
perhaps you were bountiful to me before I even asked; of this I am certain: with you there is neither delay nor excuse.
What excuse, then, have I for withholding from your praise its due, when I proclaim your bounty both in secret and in the open?
I will tell of the kindnesses you have shown me — kindnesses that lighten my debt, though they have bent my back.
sentences.n: Duban's own praise-poem, recited as he enters — unaware that the king has already resolved on his death. Line 1 is elliptical (a conditional whose apodosis is left to be inferred). The edition's own vocalisation omits the hamza mark throughout this poem wherever Classical spelling would place one on an alif seat (اَتِمَّ, اَعْدَدْتُ, بِانْعُمِ, اَتَيَقَّنُ, وَاِنَّنِي, سَاَذْكُرُ, اَوْلَيْتَنِي, وَاِنْ, اَطَالَتْ); reproduced here exactly as printed, per the edition's own verse convention, rather than corrected.

sentences.t: وَأَيْضًا فِي الْمَعْنَى
sentences.tr: wa-ayḍan fī al-maʿnā
sentences.l: And also to this effect:
sentences.i: And also, to this effect:

sentences.t:
كُنْ عَنْ هُمُومِكَ مُعْرِضًا * وَكِلِ الْاُمُورَ عَلَى الْقَضَا
وَابْشِرْ بِخَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ * تَنْسَى بِهِ مَا قَدْ مَضَى
فَلَرُبَّ اَمْرٍ مُتْعِبٍ * لَكَ فِي عَوَاقِبِهِ رِضَا
اَللّٰهُ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَا * فَلَا تَكُنْ مُتَعَرِضَا
sentences.tr:
kun ʿan humūmika muʿriḍan * wa-kili al-umūra ʿalā al-qaḍā
wa-abshir bi-khayrin ʿājilin * tansā bihi mā qad maḍā
fa-la-rubba amrin mutʿibin * laka fī ʿawāqibihi riḍā
Allāhu yafʿalu mā yashā * fa-lā takun mutaʿaraḍā
sentences.l:
Be one who turns away from your cares, and entrust all matters to fate.
And rejoice in a swift good, by which you will forget what has already passed.
For how many a wearisome matter holds, in its outcomes, contentment for you!
God does what He wills, so do not set yourself in opposition.
sentences.n: A well-known gnomic quatrain on submission to fate, rhyming throughout on -aḍā/-aḍī. مُتَعَرِضَا is printed with a single ر, where the form-V verb تَعَرَّضَ 'to oppose, set oneself against' would call for a doubled ر (mutaʿarriḍā); reproduced exactly as printed rather than corrected. اَللّٰهُ carries the edition's dagger-alif ligature over the doubled lām, as elsewhere in this text's verse.

sentences.t: وَقَٰلَ أَيْضًا فِي الْمَعْنَى
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ayḍan fī al-maʿnā
sentences.l: And he also said, to this effect:
sentences.i: And he also said, to this effect:
sentences.n: The edition again prints قل for qāla; pointed with a dagger alif as above.

sentences.t:
سَلِّمْ اُمُورَكَ لِلَّطِيفِ الْعَالِمِ * وَارِحْ فُؤَادَكَ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْعَالَمِ
وَاعْلَمْ بِاَنَّ الْاَمْرَ لَيْسَ كَمَا تَشَا * بَلْ مَا يَشَاءُ اللّٰهُ اَحْكَمُ حَاكِمِ
sentences.tr:
sallim umūraka li-al-laṭīfi al-ʿālimi * wa-ariḥ fuʾādaka min jamīʿi al-ʿālami
wa-iʿlam bi-anna al-amra laysa kamā tashā * bal mā yashāʾu Allāhu aḥkamu ḥākimi
sentences.l:
Surrender your affairs to the Subtle, the All-Knowing, and give your heart rest from the whole world.
And know that the matter is not as you wish; rather, what God wills — He is the wisest of all who judge.
sentences.i:
Commit your affairs to the Subtle, the All-Knowing, and set your heart at ease from all the world.
Know that things are not as you would have them, but as God wills — and He is the wisest of all judges.
sentences.n: الْعَالِمِ, 'the All-Knowing' (a divine epithet), and الْعَالَمِ, 'the world', form a jinās (paronomasia) at the rhyme, differing only in a single vowel. اَحْكَمُ حَاكِمِ, 'the most judicious of all who judge', is an elative followed by its own noun in the genitive, an intensifying construction ('the most X of Xers').

sentences.t: وَقَالَ أَيْضًا فِي الْمَعْنَى
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ayḍan fī al-maʿnā
sentences.l: And he also said, to this effect:

sentences.t:
طِبْ وَانْشَرِحْ وَانْسَ الْهُمُومَ جَمِيعَهَا * اِنَّ الْهُمُومَ تُزِيلُ لُبَّ الْحَازِمِ
لَا يَنْفَعُ التَّدْبِيرُ عَبْدًا عَاجِزًا * فَاتْرُكْهُ تَسَلَّمْ فِي نَعِيمٍ دَائِمِ
sentences.tr:
ṭib wa-inshariḥ wa-insa al-humūma jamīʿahā * inna al-humūma tuzīlu lubba al-ḥāzimi
lā yanfaʿu al-tadbīru ʿabdan ʿājizan * fa-utrukhu tasallam fī naʿīmin dāʾimi
sentences.l:
Be well and take heart, and forget your cares entirely; indeed, cares strip away even the resolute man's wits.
Scheming avails a helpless servant nothing; so leave it, and you will find safety in everlasting bliss.
sentences.i:
Be at ease and take heart, and put every care from your mind; for cares can rob even the most resolute man of his wits.
Contrivance profits a helpless servant nothing; let it be, and you shall find peace in unending bliss.
sentences.n: لُبّ, properly 'kernel, pith', stands here for the rational faculty, 'the mind, the wit'. فَاتْرُكْهُ تَسَلَّمْ, literally 'so leave it, [and] you will be safe', is a paratactic conditional: two juxtaposed jussives standing for 'if you leave it, you will be safe.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ لِلْحَكِيمِ دُوبَانَ أَتَعْلَمُ لِمَا ذَا أَحْضَرْتُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku li-al-ḥakīmi Dūbāna a-taʿlamu li-mā dhā aḥḍartuka
sentences.l: So the king said to the sage Duban: Do you know why I have brought you?
sentences.i: The king said to the sage Duban: Do you know why I have summoned you here?
sentences.n: لِمَا ذَا is printed as two words, as elsewhere in this edition, rather than the single modern limādhā; kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَكِيمُ لَا يَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥakīmu lā yaʿlamu al-ghayba illā Allāhu taʿālā
sentences.l: So the sage said: None knows the unseen but God, exalted is He.
sentences.i: The sage answered: None knows the unseen save God Most High.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ أَحْضَرْتُكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ وَاعْلَمْ رُوحَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-maliku aḥḍartuka li-aqtulaka wa-iʿlam rūḥaka
sentences.l: So the king said to him: I have brought you here that I may kill you — so make your soul aware.
sentences.i: The king said to him: I have brought you here to kill you — so prepare your soul.
sentences.n: اعلم روحك, literally 'inform/apprise your soul' (an imperative with a direct object, rather than the more usual wa-iʿlam anna…, 'know that…'), is used idiomatically here for bracing oneself for what is coming; rendered 'prepare your soul [for death].'

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ الْحَكِيمُ دُوبَانُ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْمَقٰلَةِ غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ وَ قَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-ḥakīmu Dūbānu min tilka al-maqālati ghāyata al-ʿajabi wa-qāla
sentences.l: So the sage Duban was astonished at that speech to the utmost degree of astonishment, and said:
sentences.i: The sage Duban was utterly astonished at those words, and said,
sentences.n: الْمَقٰلَة spells الْمَقَالَة ('the speech, the utterance') with the medial alif dropped and marked by the dagger alif, the same defective-spelling convention used for قَالَ printed قَلْ. The bare rasm coincides with مُقْلَة, 'eyeball', but that reading does not fit; read here as الْمَقَالَة, referring to the king's words just pronounced.

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ لِمَا ذَا تَقْتُلُنِي وَ أَيُّ ذَنْبٍ بَدَا مِنِّي
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-maliku li-mā dhā taqtulunī wa-ayyu dhanbin badā minnī
sentences.l: O king, for what [reason] do you kill me, and what sin has appeared from me?
sentences.i: O King, why do you kill me? What crime of mine has come to light?
sentences.n: The source spells لِمَاذَا as two words, لِمَا ذَا.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ قَدْ قِيلَ لِي إِنَّكَ جَاسُوسٌ وَ قَدْ أَتَيْتَ تَقْتُلُنِي وَ هَا أَنَا أَقْتُلُكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقْتُلَنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-maliku qad qīla lī innaka jāsūsun wa-qad atayta taqtulunī wa-hā anā aqtuluka qabla an taqtulanī
sentences.l: The king said to him: 'It has been said to me that you are a spy, and that you have come to kill me; and here I am, I kill you before you kill me.'
sentences.i: The king said to him, 'I have been told that you are a spy who has come here to kill me; so here I am — I will kill you before you can kill me.'
sentences.n: تَقْتُلُنِي here carries future/intent force although grammatically a plain indicative imperfect, a paratactic construction typical of this Middle Arabic register.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ صَاحَ عَلَى السَّيَّافِ وَ قَالَ لَهُ اِضْرِبْ رَقَبَةَ هَذَا الْغَدَّارِ وَ أَرِحْنَا مِنْ شَرِّهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika ṣāḥa ʿalā al-sayyāfi wa-qāla lahu iḍrib raqabata hādhā al-ghaddāri wa-ariḥnā min sharrihi
sentences.l: Then the king cried out to the executioner, and said to him: 'Strike the neck of this traitor, and give us rest from his evil.'
sentences.i: Then the king cried out to the executioner and said to him, 'Strike off this traitor's head, and rid us of his mischief.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَكِيمُ لِلْمَلِكِ أَبْقِنِي يُبْقِكَ اللَّهُ وَ لَا تَقْتُلْنِي يَقْتُلْكَ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥakīmu lil-maliki abqinī yubqika Allāhu wa-lā taqtulnī yaqtulka Allāhu
sentences.l: The sage said to the king: 'Spare me, [and] God will spare you; and do not kill me, [or] God will kill you.'
sentences.i: The sage said to the king, 'Spare me, and God will spare you; do not kill me, or God will kill you.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ كَرَّ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلَ مِثْلَ مَا قُلْتُ لَكَ أَيُّهَا الْعِفْرِيتُ وَ أَنْتَ لَا تَدَعُنِي إِلَّا تُرِيدُ قَتْلِي
sentences.tr: thumma innahu karra ʿalayhi al-qawla mithla mā qultu laka ayyuhā al-ʿifrītu wa-anta lā tadaʿunī illā turīdu qatlī
sentences.l: Then he repeated the same words to him — just as I said to you, O efrit, and you would not leave me be except you wanted to kill me.
sentences.i: Then he said the very same words to him again — just as I told you before, O efrit: you, too, would not let me be, except you meant to kill me.
sentences.n: From 'just as I said to you' onward, this is the fisherman's own aside to the efrit he is telling the story to, recalling his own earlier plea and the efrit's refusal in the frame narrative, not part of the tale of Duban and King Yunan.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ يُونَانُ لِلْحَكِيمِ دُوبَانَ إِنِّي لَا آمَنُ إِلَّا أَنْ أَقْتُلَكَ فَإِنَّكَ أَبْرَأْتَنِي بِشَيْءٍ مَسَكْتُهُ بِيَدِي فَلَا آمَنُ أَنْ تَقْتُلَنِي بِشَيْءٍ أَشُمُّهُ أَوْ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku Yūnānu lil-ḥakīmi Dūbāna innī lā āmanu illā an aqtulaka fa-innaka abraʾtanī bi-shayʾin masaktuhu bi-yadī fa-lā āmanu an taqtulanī bi-shayʾin ashummuhu aw ghayra dhālika
sentences.l: King Yunan said to the physician Duban: 'I am not safe unless I kill you; for you cured me with a thing I grasped in my hand, so I am not safe that you might kill me with a thing I smell, or by other than that.'
sentences.i: King Yunan said to the physician Duban, 'I can feel safe only if I kill you — for you cured me with something I merely held in my hand, so how can I feel safe that you might not kill me with something merely smelled, or by some other means?'
sentences.n: This is the king's own statement of the fear driving the whole episode.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَكِيمُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ هَذَا جَزَائِي مِنْكَ تُقَابِلُ الْمَلِيحَ بِالْقَبِيحِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥakīmu ayyuhā al-maliku hādhā jazāʾī minka tuqābilu al-malīḥa bi-al-qabīḥi
sentences.l: The sage said: 'O king, this is my recompense from you: you requite the fair with the foul.'
sentences.i: The sage said, 'O King, is this my reward from you? You repay good with evil.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ لَابُدَّ مِنْ قَتْلِكَ مِنْ غَيْرِ مُهْلَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku lā budda min qatlika min ghayri muhlatin
sentences.l: The king said: 'There is no escape from your killing, without delay.'
sentences.i: The king said, 'You must be killed, without delay.'

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَحَقَّقَ الْحَكِيمُ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ قَاتِلُهُ لَا مَحَالَةَ بَكَى وَ تَأَسَّفَ عَلَى مَا صَنَعَ مِنَ الْجَمِيلِ مَعَ غَيْرِ أَهْلِهِ كَمَا قَالَ فِي الْمَعْنَى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā taḥaqqaqa al-ḥakīmu anna al-malika qātiluhu lā maḥālata bakā wa-taʾassafa ʿalā mā ṣanaʿa mina al-jamīli maʿa ghayri ahlihi ka-mā qāla fī al-maʿnā
sentences.l: So when the sage was certain that the king would surely kill him, he wept, and grieved over the kindness he had done to other than its [rightful] people, as it was said on the theme:
sentences.i: When the sage became certain that the king would surely kill him, he wept, and mourned the kindness he had wasted on one unworthy of it — as has been said on this very theme:
sentences.n: 'Other than its [rightful] people' means someone undeserving of it. كَمَا قَالَ فِي الْمَعْنَى is a narratorial aside introducing the following anonymous verse, not spoken by Duban himself.

sentences.t:
اِنَّ مَيْمُونَةَ لَا عَقْلَ لَهَا ثِقَهْ * وَابُوهَا مِنْ ذَوِي الْعَقْلِ خُلِقْ
مَا مَشَى فِي يَابِسٍ اَوْ زلق * مِنْ غَيْرِ تَدْبِيْرٍ اِلَّا زَلِقْ
sentences.tr:
inna Maymūnata lā ʿaqla lahā thiqah * wa-abūhā min dhawī al-ʿaqli khuliq
mā mashā fī yābisin aw zalaq * min ghayri tadbīrin illā zaliq
sentences.l: Verily Maymuna has no sense, [yet she is] trusted, while her father was created among the people of sense. / No one walks on dry ground or on slippery [ground], without forethought, but he slips.
sentences.i: Maymuna has no sense at all, yet she is trusted — though her father was born a man of judgment. / No one crosses firm ground or slippery ground without forethought, but he stumbles.
sentences.n: An anonymous gnomic couplet, introduced by the narrator's own aside, not spoken by Duban himself. Maymūna is otherwise unidentified, a stock example of misplaced trust; the second line generalizes the point to anyone who acts without forethought, fitting Duban's own regret. This is the edition's own vocalisation, reproduced exactly as printed; the first زلق (before the caesura) is left undotted in the source itself, unlike its rhyme-twin زَلِقْ.

sentences.t: وَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ تَقَدَّمَ السَّيَّافُ وَ عَصَبَ عَيْنَيْهِ وَ أَشْهَرَ سَيْفَهُ وَ قَٰلَ إِذَنْ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika taqaddama al-sayyāfu wa-ʿaṣaba ʿaynayhi wa-ashhara sayfahu wa-qāla idhan
sentences.l: And after that the executioner came forward, and blindfolded his two eyes, and drew his sword, and said: 'Now then!'
sentences.i: After that the executioner stepped forward, bound Duban's eyes, drew his sword, and said, 'Now then!'
sentences.n: إِذَنْ here is the executioner's brief exclamation of readiness rather than a logical connective.

sentences.t: وَ الْحَكِيمُ يَبْكِي وَ يَقُولُ لِلْمَلِكِ أَبْقِنِي يُبْقِكَ اللَّهُ وَ لَا تَقْتُلْنِي يَقْتُلْكَ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ḥakīmu yabkī wa-yaqūlu lil-maliki abqinī yubqika Allāhu wa-lā taqtulnī yaqtulka Allāhu
sentences.l: while the sage was weeping and saying to the king: 'Spare me, [and] God will spare you; and do not kill me, [or] God will kill you.'
sentences.i: while the sage wept, saying to the king, 'Spare me, and God will spare you; do not kill me, or God will kill you.'

sentences.t: وَ أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: and he recited, saying:
sentences.i: and he recited these lines:
sentences.n: Unlike the earlier verse, introduced by the narrator's aside, this one is explicitly marked as Duban's own recitation, by وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ.

sentences.t:
تَنَصَّحْتُ فَلَمْ اُفْلِحْ وَخَانُوْا فَاَفْلَحُوْا * وَاَوْثَقَنِيْ نُصْحِيْ لِدَارِ هَوَانِ
فَاِنْ عِشْتُ لَمْ اَنْصَحْ وَاِنْ مُتُّ فَالْعَنُوْا * ذَوِي النُّصْحِ مِنْ بَعْدِيْ بِكُلِّ لِسَانِ
sentences.tr:
tanaṣṣaḥtu fa-lam uflih wa-khānū fa-aflaḥū * wa-awthaqanī nuṣḥī li-dāri hawāni
fa-in ʿishtu lam anṣaḥ wa-in muttu fa-al-ʿanū * dhawī al-nuṣḥi min baʿdī bi-kulli lisāni
sentences.l: I gave sincere counsel and did not prosper, while they betrayed and prospered; and my sincere-counsel bound me fast to a house of abasement. / So if I live, I will not counsel; and if I die, then curse, after me, the people of sincere-counsel, with every tongue.
sentences.i: I gave honest counsel and did not prosper, while the treacherous betrayed and prospered; my very honesty delivered me into a house of humiliation. / So if I live, I will counsel no one again; and if I die, then let every tongue curse, after me, all who give honest counsel.
sentences.n: Duban's own lament, explicitly marked as his own recitation, unlike the earlier anonymous couplet. This is the edition's own vocalisation, reproduced exactly as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْحَكِيمَ قَالَ لِلْمَلِكِ هَذَا جَزَائِي مِنْكَ تُجَازِينِي مُجَازَاةَ التِّمْسَاحِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ḥakīma qāla lil-maliki hādhā jazāʾī minka tujāzīnī mujāzāta al-timsāḥi
sentences.l: Then the sage said to the king: 'This is my recompense from you — you repay me the repayment of the crocodile.'
sentences.i: Then the sage said to the king, 'So this is my reward from you: you repay me as the crocodile was repaid.'
sentences.n: A proverbial comparison invoking a fable about ingratitude toward the crocodile that this text does not otherwise supply; translated literally, not filled in with invented fable details.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْمَلِكُ وَمَا
sentences.tr: qāla al-maliku wa-mā
sentences.l: The king said: 'And what…?'
sentences.i: The king said, 'And what do you mean?'
sentences.n: An elliptical interruption; the source gives only 'and what', the expected pronoun left unspoken.

sentences.t: حَتَّى إِذَا اِسْتَرَاحَ قَالَ الْحَكِيمُ لَا يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أُفَارِقَهَا وَأَنَا فِي هَذَا الْمَحَلِّ فَبِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ أَبْقِنِي يُبْقِكَ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: ḥattā idhā istarāḥa qāla al-ḥakīmu lā yumkinunī an ufāriqahā wa-anā fī hādhā al-maḥalli fa-bi-Allāhi ʿalayka abqinī yubqika Allāhu
sentences.l: until, when he had recovered, the sage said: 'It is not possible for me to part with it while I am in this plight; so by God, I adjure you: spare me, [and] God will spare you.'
sentences.i: until, when he had caught his breath, the sage said, 'I cannot part with it while I am in this plight — so, by God, I beg you: spare me, and God will spare you.'
sentences.n: 'It' refers back to the story of the crocodile just mentioned; it is left ambiguous whether 'he had recovered' refers to the king or to Duban catching his breath.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْحَكِيمَ بَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ḥakīma bakā bukāʾan shadīdan
sentences.l: Then the sage wept a violent weeping.
sentences.i: Then the sage wept bitterly.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ بَعْضُ خَوَاصِّ الْمَلِكِ وَقَالَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ هَبْ لِي دَمَ هَذَا الْحَكِيمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma baʿḍu khawāṣṣi al-maliki wa-qāla ayyuhā al-maliku hab lī dama hādhā al-ḥakīmi
sentences.l: Then one of the king's intimates rose up, and said: 'O king, grant me the blood of this sage.'
sentences.i: Then one of the king's own courtiers rose up and said, 'O King, spare this sage's life for my sake.'
sentences.n: 'Grant me his blood' is the idiom for begging that a condemned man's life be spared as a personal favor to the speaker.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّنَا مَا رَأَيْنَا فَعَلَ ذَنْبًا وَمَا رَأَيْنَا إِلَّا أَبْرَأَكَ مِنْ مَرَضِكَ الَّذِي أَعْيَى الْأَطِبَّاءَ وَالْحُكَمَاءَ
sentences.tr: li-annanā mā raʾaynā faʿala dhanban wa-mā raʾaynā illā abraʾaka min maraḍika alladhī aʿyā al-aṭibbāʾa wa-al-ḥukamāʾa
sentences.l: for we have not seen [him] commit a sin, and we have not seen [anything] except [that] he cured you of your illness which had wearied the physicians and the sages.
sentences.i: for we have never seen him do wrong — we have seen him do nothing but cure you of the illness that had defeated every physician and sage.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْمَلِكُ لَمْ تَعْرِفُوا سَبَبَ قَتْلِي هَذَا الْحَكِيمَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-maliku lam taʿrifū sababa qatlī hādhā al-ḥakīma
sentences.l: The king said to them: 'You do not know the reason for my killing this sage.'
sentences.i: The king said to them, 'You do not understand my reason for killing this sage.'

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ لِأَنِّي إِنْ أَبْقَيْتُهُ فَأَنَا هَالِكٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika li-annī in abqaytuhu fa-anā hālikun lā maḥālata
sentences.l: And that is because, if I let him remain, then I am perishing without escape.
sentences.i: It is because, if I let him live, I am doomed without fail.

sentences.t: وَمَنْ أَبْرَأَنِي مِنَ الْمَرَضِ الَّذِي كَانَ بِي بِشَيْءٍ أَشُمُّهُ بِيَدِي فَيُمْكِنُ أَنْ يَقْتُلَنِي بِشَيْءٍ أَشُمُّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-man abraʾanī mina al-maraḍi alladhī kāna bī bi-shayʾin ashummuhu bi-yadī fa-yumkinu an yaqtulanī bi-shayʾin ashummuhu
sentences.l: For one who cured me of the illness that was in me with a thing I smell with my hand, it is possible that he kill me with a thing I smell.
sentences.i: A man who could cure me of the illness in me with something I merely smell in my hand could just as easily kill me with something smelled.
sentences.n: The source repeats أَشُمُّهُ ('I smell it') here, where the parallel with the king's earlier reasoning would lead one to expect a verb of touching or holding; this looks like a dittography anticipating the following clause rather than a deliberate repetition, but the letters are reproduced exactly as printed.

sentences.t: فَأَنَا أَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلَنِي وَيَأْخُذَ عَلَى اِبْرِطِيلٍ لِأَنَّهُ جَاسُوسٌ وَمَا جَاءَ إِلَّا لِيَقْتُلَنِي فَلَابُدَّ مِنْ قَتْلِهِ وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ آمَنُ عَلَى نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-anā akhāfu an yaqtulanī wa-yaʾkhudha ʿalā ibriṭīlin li-annahu jāsūsun wa-mā jāʾa illā li-yaqtulanī fa-lā budda min qatlihi wa-baʿda dhālika āmanu ʿalā nafsī
sentences.l: So I fear that he kill me and take, for it, a bribe, because he is a spy and has not come except to kill me; so there is no escape from killing him, and after that I shall be safe for myself.
sentences.i: So I fear he may kill me and be paid a bribe for it, since he is a spy who has come for no purpose but to kill me; he must be killed, and only then will I feel safe.
sentences.n: اِبْرِطِيل, apparently a colloquial pronunciation of Classical بِرْطِيل, 'bribe', pictures Duban as a hired assassin; the exact construction with عَلَى is compressed and not fully certain, but the general sense is clear from context.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَكِيمُ أَبْقِنِي يُبْقِكَ اللَّهُ وَلَا تَقْتُلْنِي يَقْتُلْكَ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥakīmu abqinī yubqika Allāhu wa-lā taqtulnī yaqtulka Allāhu
sentences.l: The sage said: 'Spare me, [and] God will spare you; and do not kill me, [or] God will kill you.'
sentences.i: The sage said, 'Spare me, and God will spare you; do not kill me, or God will kill you.'

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَحَقَّقَ الْحَكِيمُ — أَيُّهَا الْعِفْرِيتُ — أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ قَاتِلُهُ لَا مَحَالَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā taḥaqqaqa al-ḥakīmu — ayyuhā al-ʿifrītu — anna al-malika qātiluhu lā maḥālata
sentences.l: So when the sage became certain — O efrit — that the king would surely kill him,
sentences.i: So when the sage became certain — O efrit! — that the king was bound to kill him,
sentences.n: 'O efrit' is the fisherman's own frame-narration voice breaking into the tale to address the efrit he is telling it to, exactly as at the tale's opening; not part of Duban's or the king's speech, set off here as a parenthetical.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنْ كَانَ وَلَابُدَّ مِنْ قَتْلِي فَأَمْهِلْنِي أَنْ أَنْزِلَ إِلَى دَارِي
sentences.tr: qāla lahu ayyuhā al-maliku in kāna wa-lā budda min qatlī fa-amhilnī an anzila ilā dārī
sentences.l: he said to him: 'O king, if it must be that there is no escape from my killing, then grant me respite that I may go down to my house,'
sentences.i: he said to him, 'O King, if I must indeed be killed, then grant me a little time to go home,'

sentences.t: وَأُوْصِيَ أَهْلِي وَجِيرَانِي يَدْفِنُونِي وَأُبَرِّيَ نَفْسِي وَأَهَبَ كُتُبَ الطِّبِّ
sentences.tr: wa-ūṣiya ahlī wa-jīrānī yadfinūnī wa-ubarriya nafsī wa-ahaba kutuba al-ṭibbi
sentences.l: and that I instruct my family and my neighbors [that] they bury me, and settle my own affairs, and give away the books of medicine,
sentences.i: and instruct my family and my neighbors to see to my burial, settle my affairs, and give away my medical books,
sentences.n: وَأُبَرِّيَ نَفْسِي is printed with a plain ي where أُبَرِّئَ نَفْسِي would carry a hamza — the same defective yāʾ-for-hamza spelling seen elsewhere in this printing; read here as Form II, 'settle my own affairs' before death.

sentences.t: وَعِنْدِي كِتَابٌ خَاصٌّ أُهْدِيهِ لَكَ هَدِيَّةً تَدَّخِرُهُ فِي خِزَانَتِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿindī kitābun khāṣṣun uhdīhi laka hadiyyatan taddakhiruhu fī khizānatika
sentences.l: and I have a special book [which] I present to you as a gift, [that] you may store it in your treasury.
sentences.i: and I have one especially valuable book which I will give you as a parting gift, for you to keep in your treasury.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ لِلْحَكِيمِ وَمَا فِي ذَلِكَ الْكِتَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku lil-ḥakīmi wa-mā fī dhālika al-kitābi
sentences.l: So the king said to the sage, 'And what is in that book?'

sentences.t: قَالَ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ لَا يُحْصَى
sentences.tr: qāla fīhi shayʾun lā yuḥṣā
sentences.l: He said, 'In it is a thing that cannot be counted.'
