sentences.i: He said, 'In it is more than can ever be counted.'

sentences.t: وَأَقَلُّ مَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْأَسْرَارِ أَنَّكَ إِذَا قَطَعْتَ رَأْسِي وَفَتَحْتَ ثَلَٰثَ وَرَقَاتٍ وَتَقْرَأُ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَسْطُرٍ مِنَ الصَّفْحَةِ الَّتِي عَلَى يَسَارِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-aqallu mā fīhi mina al-asrāri annaka idhā qaṭaʿta raʾsī wa-fataḥta thalātha waraqātin wa-taqraʾu thalāthata asṭurin mina al-ṣafḥati allatī ʿalā yasārika
sentences.l: And the least of what is in it, of the secrets, is that you — when you have cut off my head, and opened three leaves, and read three lines from the page that is on your left —
sentences.i: And the least of its secrets is this: when you have cut off my head, opened three leaves, and read three lines from the page on your left,
sentences.n: ثَلَٰثَ and ثَلَٰثَةَ spell Classical ثَلَاثَ/ثَلَاثَةَ without the medial alif; a dagger alif marks the elided long vowel, the same defective-spelling convention already used for قَٰلَ elsewhere in this text.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ الرَّأْسَ يُكَلِّمُكَ وَيُجَاوِبُكَ بِجَمِيعِ مَا سَأَلْتَهُ عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-raʾsa yukallimuka wa-yujāwibuka bi-jamīʿi mā saʾaltahu ʿanhu
sentences.l: — then indeed the head will speak to you, and answer you concerning everything you have asked it.
sentences.i: — then the head will speak to you, and answer you on whatever you ask it.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ الْمَلِكُ غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ وَاِهْتَزَّ مِنَ الطَّرَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-maliku ghāyata al-ʿajabi wa-ihtazza mina al-ṭarabi
sentences.l: Then the king marveled the utmost of marveling, and was thrilled with delight.
sentences.i: The king was utterly astonished, and thrilled through with delight.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الْحَكِيمُ إِذَا قَطَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ تُكَلِّمُنِي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu ayyuhā al-ḥakīmu idhā qaṭaʿta raʾsaka tukallimunī
sentences.l: And he said to him, 'O sage, if I cut off your head, will you speak to me?'

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam ayyuhā al-maliku
sentences.l: He said, 'Yes, O King.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ هَذَا أَمْرٌ عَجِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku hādhā amrun ʿajībun
sentences.l: The king said, 'This is an amazing thing.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَرْسَلَهُ فِي التَّرْسِيمِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika arsalahu fī al-tarsīmi
sentences.l: Then the king sent him off under guard.
sentences.n: التَّرْسِيمِ names the condition the king had already put Duban under when he first reprieved him; it recurs at the next day's court, where Duban stands 'قُدَّامَ الْمَلِكِ فِي التَّرْسِيمِ', 'before the king, still under guard.'

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ الْحَكِيمُ إِلَى دَارِهِ وَقَضَى أَشْغَالَهُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala al-ḥakīmu ilā dārihi wa-qaḍā ashghālahu fī dhālika al-yawmi
sentences.l: So the sage went down to his house, and settled his affairs on that day.

sentences.t: وَفِي الْيَوْمِ الثَّانِي طَلَعَ الْحَكِيمُ إِلَى الدِّيوَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-yawmi al-thānī ṭalaʿa al-ḥakīmu ilā al-dīwāni
sentences.l: And on the second day the sage went up to the council-hall.

sentences.t: وَطَلَعَتِ الْأُمَرَاءُ وَ الْوُزَرَاءُ وَالْحُجَّابُ وَالنُّوَّابُ وَأَرْبَابُ الدَّوْلَةِ جَمِيعًا
sentences.tr: wa-ṭalaʿati al-umarāʾu wa-al-wuzarāʾu wa-al-ḥujjābu wa-al-nuwwābu wa-arbābu al-dawlati jamīʿan
sentences.l: And the emirs, and the viziers, and the chamberlains, and the deputies, and the lords of the state went up, all of them,
sentences.i: and the emirs, viziers, chamberlains, deputies, and the great officers of the state all came up together,

sentences.t: وَحَارَ الدِّيوَانُ كَزَهْرِ الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥāra al-dīwānu ka-zahri al-bustāni
sentences.l: and the council-hall was dazzled/bewildered like the flower of the garden.
sentences.i: and the hall shone as bright as a garden in bloom.
sentences.n: حَارَ ordinarily means 'to be bewildered, confounded', not 'to shine'; vocalised on its own most natural sense, extended figuratively. A reviewer may prefer a corruption of زَهَا ('to be resplendent'), punning with the following كَزَهْرِ; letters reproduced exactly as printed.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْحَكِيمِ طَلَعَ لِلدِّيوَانِ وَوَقَفَ قُدَّامَ الْمَلِكِ فِي التَّرْسِيمِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-ḥakīmi ṭalaʿa lil-dīwāni wa-waqafa quddāma al-maliki fī al-tarsīmi
sentences.l: And then, there was the sage: he went up to the council-hall and stood before the king, under guard,
sentences.i: And then, there was the sage — he came up into the hall and stood before the king, still under guard,

sentences.t: وَمَعَهُ كِتَابٌ عَتِيقٌ وَسِلْسِلَةٌ فِيهَا ذَرُورٌ
sentences.tr: wa-maʿahu kitābun ʿatīqun wa-silsilatun fīhā dharūrun
sentences.l: having with him an ancient book, and a chain in which was some powder.
sentences.i: carrying with him an ancient book, and a small chained case holding some powder.
sentences.n: سِلْسِلَة normally means 'chain'; an odd vessel for powder — may stand for a small chained box/pouch, or be a compositor's error for سُلَّة ('basket'). Reproduced exactly as printed.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسَ وَقَٰلَ اِئْتُونِي بِطَبَقٍ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasa wa-qāla ītūnī bi-ṭabaqin
sentences.l: and he sat down, and said, 'Bring me a dish.'

sentences.t: فَأَتَوْهُ بِطَبَقٍ
sentences.tr: fa-atawhu bi-ṭabaqin
sentences.l: So they brought him a dish.

sentences.t: وَكَبَّ فِيهِ الذَّرُورَ وَفَرَشَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kabba fīhi al-dharūra wa-farashahu
sentences.l: And he poured the powder into it, and spread it out,

sentences.t: وَقَٰلَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ خُذْ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ayyuhā al-maliku khudh hādhā al-kitāba
sentences.l: and said, 'O King, take this book,

sentences.t: وَلَا تَفْتَحْهُ حَتَّى تَقْطَعَ رَأْسِي
sentences.tr: wa-lā taftaḥhu ḥattā taqṭaʿa raʾsī
sentences.l: and do not open it until you have cut off my head.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا قَطَعْتَهُ فَاِجْعَلْهُ فِي ذَلِكَ الطَّبَقِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā qaṭaʿtahu fa-ijʿalhu fī dhālika al-ṭabaqi
sentences.l: Then when you have cut it off, put it on that dish,

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ بِكَبْسِهِ عَلَى ذَلِكَ الذَّرُورِ
sentences.tr: wa-amara bi-kabsihi ʿalā dhālika al-dharūri
sentences.l: and he directed that it be pressed down onto that powder.
sentences.i: and give orders that it be pressed down onto that powder.
sentences.n: Where the preceding instructions run as direct imperatives, وَأَمَرَ shifts to a narrated perfect ('and he ordered'); kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا فَعَلْتَ ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّ دَمَهُ يَنْقَطِعُ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā faʿalta dhālika fa-inna damahu yanqaṭiʿu
sentences.l: Then when you have done that, its blood will indeed stop.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اِفْتَحِ الْكِتَابَ
sentences.tr: thumma iftaḥi al-kitāba
sentences.l: Then open the book.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَمَرَ بِضَرْبِ رَقَبَتِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika amara bi-ḍarbi raqabatihi
sentences.l: Then the king commanded that his neck be struck,

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ وَقَامَ السَّيَّافُ وَضَرَبَ رَقَبَتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-kitāba minhu wa-qāma al-sayyāfu wa-ḍaraba raqabatahu
sentences.l: so he took the book from him, and the executioner rose and struck his neck,

sentences.t: فَطَاحَ الرَّأْسُ فِي وَسَطِ الطَّبَقِ وَكَبَسَهُ عَلَى الذَّرُورِ فَاِنْقَطَعَ دَمُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭāḥa al-raʾsu fī wasaṭi al-ṭabaqi wa-kabasahu ʿalā al-dharūri fa-inqaṭaʿa damuhu
sentences.l: and the head fell into the middle of the dish, and it was pressed onto the powder, and its blood stopped.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَ الْحَكِيمُ دُوبَانُ عَيْنَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥa al-ḥakīmu Dūbānu ʿaynayhi
sentences.l: Then the sage Duban opened his two eyes

sentences.t: وَقَٰلَ اِفْتَحِ الْكِتَابَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla iftaḥi al-kitāba ayyuhā al-maliku
sentences.l: and said, 'Open the book, O King.'

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَهُ الْمَلِكُ فَوَجَدَهُ مَلْصُوقًا
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥahu al-maliku fa-wajadahu malṣūqan
sentences.l: So the king opened it, and found it stuck together.

sentences.t: فَحَطَّ إِصْبَعَهُ فِي فَمِهِ وَعَمِلَ رِيقَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaṭṭa iṣbaʿahu fī famihi wa-ʿamila rīqahu
sentences.l: So he put his finger into his mouth and worked it with his spittle,
sentences.i: So he put his finger to his mouth and wetted it with his own spittle,

sentences.t: وَفَتَحَ أَوَّلَ وَرَقَةٍ وَ الْوَرَقُ مَا يَنْفَتِحُ إِلَّا بِجَهْدٍ
sentences.tr: wa-fataḥa awwala waraqatin wa-al-waraqu mā yanfatiḥu illā bi-jahdin
sentences.l: and opened the first leaf — the leaves would not open except with effort.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَ الْمَلِكُ سِتَّةَ أَوْرَاقٍ وَنَظَرَ فِيهَا فَلَمْ يَجِدْ فِيهَا كِتَابَةً
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥa al-maliku sittata awrāqin wa-naẓara fīhā fa-lam yajid fīhā kitābatan
sentences.l: Then the king opened six leaves and looked into them, and found no writing in them,

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ أَيُّهَا الْحَكِيمُ مَا فِيهِ شَيٌ مَكْتُوبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku ayyuhā al-ḥakīmu mā fīhi shayun maktūbun
sentences.l: and the king said, 'O sage, there is nothing written in it.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَكِيمُ اِفْتَحْ زِيَادَةً عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥakīmu iftaḥ ziyādatan ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: The sage said, 'Open more, beyond that.'

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَ ثَلَٰثَةً أُخَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥa thalāthatan ukhara
sentences.l: So he opened three more,

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ مِنَ الزَّمَانِ إِلَّا وَالدَّوَاءُ حَاقَ فِيهِ لِوَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā kāna illā qalīlun mina al-zamāni illā wa-al-dawāʾu ḥāqa fīhi li-waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi
sentences.l: and it was but a little while of time before the drug had taken effect in him then and there,
sentences.i: and it was only a little while before the poison had already taken hold in him,
sentences.n: مَا كَانَ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ...إِلَّا وَ... is the idiom 'no sooner had a little time passed than…'.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ الْكِتَابَ كَانَ مَسْمُومًا
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-kitāba kāna masmūman
sentences.l: for the book had indeed been poisoned.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَزَعْزَعَ الْمَلِكُ وَصَاحَ وَقَالَ حَاقَ فِيَّ الدَّوَاءُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika tazaʿzaʿa al-maliku wa-ṣāḥa wa-qāla ḥāqa fiyya al-dawāʾu
sentences.l: At that the king reeled, and cried out, and said, 'The poison has taken hold in me!'
sentences.n: فِيَّ is فِي + the 1cs suffix, geminated ('in me'); unpointed, written identically to the bare preposition فِي.

sentences.t: اِنْشَلَّ الْحَكِيمُ دُوبَانُ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: inshalla al-ḥakīmu Dūbānu yaqūlu
sentences.l: The sage Duban became paralyzed(?), saying:
sentences.i: The sage Duban recited, saying:
sentences.n: اِنْشَلَّ as printed is form VII of ش-ل-ل, 'to become paralysed' — a real word but a poor fit as the verb governing 'saying' that follows. The tale elsewhere introduces a quoted poem with وَأَنْشَدَ...يَقُولُ; انشل/انشد differ by one letter (ل for د), so this is almost certainly a compositor's misreading of أَنْشَدَ, 'he recited.' Idiomatic translation follows that near-certain correction; letters reproduced exactly as printed. Flag for the scan.

sentences.t:
تَحَكَّمُوا وَاسْتَطَالُوا فِي تَحَكُّمِهِمْ * وَعَنْ قَلِيلٍ كَانَ الْحُكْمُ لَمْ يَكُنِ
لَوْ أَنْصَفُوا أَنْصَفُوا لٰكِنْ بَغَوْا فَبَغَى * عَلَيْهِمُ الدَّهْرُ بِالْأَحْزَانِ وَالْمِحَنِ
وَأَصْبَحُوا وَلِسَانُ الْحَالِ يُنْشِدُهُمْ * هٰذَا بِذَاكَ وَلَا عَتَبَ عَلَى الزَّمَنِ
sentences.tr:
taḥakkamū wa-istaṭālū fī taḥakkumihim * wa-ʿan qalīlin kāna al-ḥukmu lam yakuni
law anṣafū anṣafū lākin baghaw fa-baghā * ʿalayhimu al-dahru bi-al-aḥzāni wa-al-miḥani
wa-aṣbaḥū wa-lisānu al-ḥāli yunshiduhum * hādhā bi-dhāka wa-lā ʿataba ʿalā al-zamani
sentences.l:
They exercised absolute power, and overreached in their exercise of it * and after a little while, dominion was as though it had not been.
Had they dealt justly, they would have been dealt with justly — but they oppressed, so fate oppressed * them with griefs and trials,
and they awoke, with the tongue of circumstance reciting to them: * 'This for that, and no blame falls upon time.'
sentences.i:
They ruled, and overreached in their ruling; and in a little while their dominion was as if it had never been.
Had they dealt justly, they would have been dealt with justly — but they oppressed, and so fate turned and oppressed them in turn, with griefs and trials,
and they awoke to hear their own case declare to them: 'This for that — and time is not to blame.'
sentences.n: This closing epigram is printed already fully pointed; reproduced exactly as given, including the dagger-alif spellings لٰكِنْ and هٰذَا. Line 1 plays on كَانَ/لَمْ يَكُنْ, i.e. dominion proved short-lived. Line 2's لَوْ أَنْصَفُوا أَنْصَفُوا is elliptical (apodosis compressed by repeating the verb). لِسَانُ الْحَالِ ('the tongue of circumstance') is the idiom for a situation that 'speaks for itself'; هٰذَا بِذَاكَ, 'this for that', is the tit-for-tat formula. The three couplets are given as one continuous quoted poem since Duban's head recites them as a single uninterrupted utterance.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ رَأْسُ الْحَكِيمِ كَلَامَهُ سَقَطَ الْمَلِكُ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ مَيِّتًا
sentences.tr: qāla fa-lammā faragha raʾsu al-ḥakīmi kalāmahu saqaṭa al-maliku min waqtihi mayyitan
sentences.l: He said: Then when the sage's head had finished its speech, the king fell down dead upon the instant.

sentences.t: فَاعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْعِفْرِيتُ أَنَّهُ لَوْ أَبْقَى الْمَلِكُ يُونَانُ الْحَكِيمَ دُوبَانَ لَأَبْقَاهُ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-iʿlam ayyuhā al-ʿifrītu annahu law abqā al-maliku Yūnānu al-ḥakīma Dūbāna la-abqāhu Allāhu
sentences.l: So know, O efrit, that had King Yunan spared the sage Duban, God would have spared him,
sentences.i: So know, O efrit: had King Yunan spared the sage Duban, God would have spared him,
sentences.n: From here the fisherman speaks in his own voice directly to the efrit he has trapped — one frame level out from King Yunan's tale, which has just ended; 'know, O efrit' is addressed to the jinni, not to Shahrazad's king.

sentences.t: وَ لَكِنْ أَبَى وَطَلَبَ قَتْلَهُ فَقَتَلَهُ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin abā wa-ṭalaba qatlahu fa-qatalahu Allāhu
sentences.l: but he refused, and sought to kill him, so God killed him.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ أَيُّهَا الْعِفْرِيتُ لَوْ أَبْقَيْتَنِي لَا أَبْقَاكَ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-anta ayyuhā al-ʿifrītu law abqaytanī lā abqāka Allāhu
sentences.l: And you, O efrit — had you spared me — God did not spare you.
sentences.i: And as for you, O efrit: had you spared me, God would not have spared you.
sentences.n: The archive prints لا ابقاك with a visible word-space — read literally, the negator لَا + أَبْقَاكَ. But the preceding sentence uses the identical law…la- construction fused as one word, لَابْقَاهُ (=لَأَبْقَاهُ), and this line is generally read as its mirror ('had you spared me, God would have spared you'). It is quite possible لا ابقاك is the same لَأَبْقَاكَ construction with the hamza's bare alif simply mis-spaced by the compositor, rather than a genuine negation. Not silently emended; flagged for the reviewer to check against the scan, since the two readings are opposite in polarity.

sentences.t: فَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: Then morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent from the speech permitted [to her].
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent, having reached the end of what she was permitted to say.
